For a language that resolves a committed lockfile (cpp), it then runs that language's lock command (conan lock create . -s build_type=Debug) and one full vrg-validate inside the dev container, so the new repo is born green — it passes validation from its first commit. The container is a fail-fast precondition for a lock-resolving language: if no runtime is available the step refuses before writing anything, so such a repo is born green or not born at all, never half-created. The step writes no commit of its own; its host-rendered skeleton and container-resolved lock ride into the next step's commit. Because the container warmup for cpp requires a conan.lock and one does not yet exist during this window, the warmup deliberately skips until the scaffold's conan lock create produces the lock — the skeleton resolves in an unwarmed-but-usable container, and the warmup runs normally on every later build once the lock is committed (epic vergil-project/.github#342).

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_github_repo_init Args org/name positional; --adopt, --non-interactive, --target-dir, and per-field overrides (--language, --repository-type, …) Preconditions gh and git on PATH; run from the org-layout parent (or pass --target-dir) Failure mode Loud refusal on a foreign-repo CWD, an occupied clone path, or missing required non-interactive values Exit codes 0 success, 1 error Status Active

docs.title: vrg-gitignore-sync
docs.text:
Single-repo applicator for the vergil-managed .gitignore block. Reads <repo>/.gitignore, resolves the fence language from [project].primary-language (normalized to base-only for any language without a managed fragment), and either checks (default) or writes the composed base + <language> managed block through lib/gitignore.py — the same module the config audit renders through, so applicator and audit cannot diverge. It owns only the file change: it has no git or PR knowledge. --write rewrites the fenced block, moves it to the top of the file, and drops any exact repeat of one of the fence's own patterns outside it (the fence is the single source of truth), leaving genuinely repo-local lines untouched and in order. --check reports drift exactly when --write would change the file, so --write then --check always passes (#3568). See the GitHub Config Audit reference.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_gitignore_sync Args --repo PATH (default: CWD); mutually exclusive --check (default) | --write Preconditions A repo whose language resolves from [project].primary-language (no vergil.toml or no declared language → base-only; a vergil.toml that fails to load is an error, exit 2) Failure mode --check prints each drift reason to stderr; --write succeeds whenever the language resolves (prints already in sync or the synced path) Exit codes 0 ok, 1 --check drift, 2 usage error or a vergil.toml that fails to load (the config error is printed to stderr; nothing is written) Status Active

docs.title: vrg-dependabot-sync
docs.text:
Single-repo applicator for the canonical report-only .github/dependabot.yml (epic vergil-project/.github#420). Resolves the repo's [project].primary-language and either checks (default) or writes the render from lib/dependabot.py: a github-actions entry plus the language's ecosystem (python → uv, go → gomod, rust → cargo, java → maven, typescript → npm; any other language gets github-actions only), every entry at open-pull-requests-limit: 0 so Dependabot never opens a PR. The file is exact match: --write replaces local additions. It owns only the file change and has no git or PR knowledge.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_dependabot_sync Args --repo PATH (default: CWD); mutually exclusive --check (default) | --write Preconditions A repo whose language resolves from [project].primary-language (no vergil.toml or no declared language → github-actions only; a vergil.toml that fails to load is an error, exit 2) Failure mode --check prints missing .github/dependabot.yml or differs from the canonical render to stderr; --write succeeds whenever the language resolves (prints already in sync or wrote .github/dependabot.yml (<lang or none>)) Exit codes 0 ok, 1 --check drift, 2 usage error or a vergil.toml that fails to load (the config error is printed to stderr; nothing is written) Status Active

docs.title: vrg-fleet-sync
docs.text:
Propagate a vergil-managed file across a fleet of repositories, opening one PR per repo whose file drifts. --target picks the file: gitignore (default) syncs the managed .gitignore block via vrg-gitignore-sync --write; dependabot writes the report-only .github/dependabot.yml via vrg-dependabot-sync --write (branch slug dependabot-config, filed under epic vergil-project/.github#420). A target's epic links only repos in the epic's own org: a repo in another org (read from the clone with gh repo view) is filed under its own ad-hoc epic, and the issue body still names the target's epic, because vrg-issue-create refuses a cross-org link. It drives the generic fleet-sweep driver (lib/fleet_sweep.py): per repo it creates a worktree, shells out to the target's applicator, commits, and runs report-ready. Like every agent-run task it never submits or merges — it stops at report-ready, leaving submission and merge to the human. --dry-run reports the verdict a live run would reach per repo (would change, naming the epic it would be filed under, or skip) from a disposable probe worktree, without opening an issue, branch, commit, or PR. Each target previews with its applicator's --check (vrg-gitignore-sync --check or vrg-dependabot-sync --check), whose drift verdict is exactly the change --write would make.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_fleet_sync Args --repos PATH [PATH …] (required, local clone paths); --target {dependabot,gitignore} (default gitignore); --dry-run Preconditions The target's applicator (vrg-gitignore-sync or vrg-dependabot-sync) on PATH; each --repos path a local clone; git/gh credentials for the sweep Failure mode Any repo that errors is recorded and reported in the per-repo status lines Exit codes 0 all repos ok, 1 one or more repos errored Status Active

docs.title: vrg-container-run
docs.text:
Run arbitrary commands inside a dev container. Auto-detects the project language to select the Docker image; falls back to dev-base:latest. Uses execvp to replace the process.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_container_run Args [--prefix <dev\|prod>] [--] <command> [args...] (manual parsing, -- separator) Preconditions Git repo, GH_TOKEN set, Docker daemon running Failure mode Explicit error message for missing GH_TOKEN; assert_docker_available() exits with message for Docker; git.repo_root() raises on non-git directory; in a cpp repo, an unreadable or malformed ConanCenter audit token source exits 1 naming the file (see Container Config) Exit codes 0 (help), 1 error; command exit code after execvp Status Active

docs.title: vrg-container-test
docs.text:
Run a repository's test suite inside a dev container. Auto-detects language and selects appropriate image and test command.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_container_test Args None Preconditions Git repo, Docker daemon running, language detection or DOCKER_DEV_IMAGE + DOCKER_TEST_CMD Failure mode Explicit error for undetected language and unavailable Docker; git.repo_root() raises on non-git directory Exit codes 0 (help), 1 error; command exit code after execvp Status Active

docs.title: vrg-container-docs
docs.text:
Preview or build MkDocs documentation inside a dev container. Supports serve (live-reload) and build subcommands. For Python repos, wraps with uv sync --group docs and sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system, so uv uses the docs image's own Python (as CI does) whatever the repo's python-preference, and fails loudly if that Python does not satisfy requires-python. Always sets NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING=1 in the container, so local builds suppress the mkdocs-material MkDocs 2.0 warning banner the same way CI does.

Before mkdocs runs, it stages the docs sources on the host the same way CI's docs job does (actions/shared/docs/stage in vergil-actions), so a local strict build passes or fails where CI's does:

  1. vrg-docs-stage copies CHANGELOG.md to <config dir>/docs/changelog.md and releases/*.md to <config dir>/docs/releases/, and writes the release index.
  2. vrg-docs-patch-nav patches the release versions into the nav of a copy of the config, mkdocs.staged.yml, written next to mkdocs.yml. The tracked mkdocs.yml is never modified. mkdocs runs with -f <config dir>/mkdocs.staged.yml.

Staging needs authenticated gh (or an App token in agent sessions) whenever the repo has release notes, because each release page links to its CI-evidence bundle. Without auth the command fails; it never skips staging.

Staging must not dirty the working tree, so every generated path has to be gitignored. The managed base gitignore covers the default layout (docs/site/docs/changelog.md, docs/site/docs/releases/, mkdocs.staged.yml). If a generated path is not ignored, including a staged copy that the repo has committed, the command refuses before writing anything and lists the paths. To fix it, stop tracking any committed copies (vrg-git rm --cached <path>), then run vrg-gitignore-sync.

serve stages once, at startup. Edits to the docs pages reload as usual, but edits to mkdocs.yml, CHANGELOG.md or releases/ take effect only after a restart.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_container_docs Args <serve\|build> [mkdocs args...] (manual parsing) Preconditions Git repo, Docker daemon, mkdocs config at MKDOCS_CONFIG (default docs/site/mkdocs.yml), generated docs paths gitignored, gh auth when the repo has release notes Failure mode Usage message on missing/unknown subcommand; explicit error for a missing config, un-ignored generated paths, or a staging failure (including missing gh auth) Exit codes 0 (help), 1 error; command exit code after execvp Status Active

docs.title: vrg-container-build-command
docs.text:
Print a repo's declared [container].build-command verbatim, for CI consumption. The CI test jobs call --script to obtain the exact provisioning command to run per job — the same command the local cache build bakes into the per-branch image — so the two paths run one declaration. Prints nothing when the repo declares no build-command. See Container Config Reference → build-command.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_container_build_command Args --script (explicit CI intent; identical output), --repo-root (default: CWD) Preconditions A readable vergil.toml at the repo root (absent/empty key prints nothing) Failure mode argparse error on unknown flags; no failure for an unset key Exit codes 0 always Status Active

docs.title: vrg-container-system-packages
docs.text:
Print a repo's declared [container].system-packages, for CI consumption. Default mode prints the package names one per line; --install-script prints the exact apt install snippet — the single speller shared with the local cache build — which the CI test jobs run. See Container Config Reference → system-packages.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_container_system_packages Args --install-script (apt snippet instead of the name list), --repo-root (default: CWD) Preconditions A readable vergil.toml at the repo root (absent/empty key prints nothing) Failure mode argparse error on unknown flags; no failure for an unset key Exit codes 0 always Status Active

docs.title: vrg-container-cache
docs.text:
Manage the per-branch cached container image (base image plus vergil-tooling, system-packages, and the build-command artifact) that vrg-container-run builds over. Subcommands: build (build/refresh the cached image for the current branch), clean (remove it), status (show cache state and the expected tag), clean-all (remove every image it manages), and prune (remove the cached images of finished branches).

prune covers every cached per-branch image in the local image store, whichever repo built it. It is a dry run by default: it prints the repo set and a keep or remove verdict, with the reason, for each image, and removes nothing until re-run with --apply (issue #3481). The image tag records the branch (sanitized: / becomes -) but not the repository, so the rule leans toward keeping. An image is kept when:

  • its branch is protected (develop, main, release);
  • a container, running or stopped, uses it;
  • its branch matches a live branch in any repo of the repo set. A branch is live when it is a local branch (which covers every worktree) or exists on the repo's origin.

Only an image that matches none of these is removed. Origin is read with git ls-remote, so a branch deleted on GitHub counts as gone. When a repo's origin cannot be read (typically a private repo the agent's App cannot see), that repo's local refs/remotes/origin/* stand in, with a warning naming the repo; stale tracking refs can only keep extra images, never remove live ones. Any other failure to read the repo set, the images, the containers or a repo's branches stops the run before anything is removed. A failed image removal is reported with the runtime's error, the remaining removals still run, and the command exits 1.

The repo set comes from --root DIR (repeatable; a projects directory, a directory of repos, or a single repo, searched down to <org>/<repo>), which replaces the platform default: /vergil/projects on a cloud VM, and on a Lima VM the projects mount, found two levels above the current repo's main worktree and accepted only if it is a mount point. The physical host has no default, so --root is required there. A root that does not exist, or roots that hold no repositories, are an error.

vrg-finalize-pr runs the same sweep (in effect prune --apply against the platform's default repo set) after removing the merged branch's own cached images. It runs on agent VMs and is skipped on the physical Mac host, which has no default repo set; there finalize prints the vrg-container-cache prune --root DIR command to run by hand. A failed sweep or removal is a finalize warning, never a failure (issue #3566).

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_container_cache Args build | clean | status | clean-all | prune [--apply] [--root DIR]... Preconditions A container runtime (nerdctl or docker) on PATH for every subcommand; a git repo for build/clean/status; for prune, a repo set (--root DIR on the physical host) Failure mode Runtime-unavailable error; propagates the runtime's build failures; every failed image removal is reported with the runtime's error while the rest still run. prune refuses, before removing anything, a missing or empty repo set, or images, containers or branches it cannot read Exit codes 0 success (including a prune dry run); 1 no subcommand, no runtime, a failed removal, or a prune refusal; non-zero on build failure Status Active

docs.title: vrg-host
docs.text:
Observe and manage the Vergil-critical macOS host dependencies (uv, gh, git, bash, gcloud, Lima, Docker Desktop, OpenTofu, git-cliff, vergil-tooling, Claude Code, macOS, the Xcode Command Line Tools) declared in the packaged, tooling-owned manifest src/vergil_tooling/data/host_dependencies.toml (never repo-overridable). status (the default) reports installed-vs-latest drift, auxiliary-check health and pins; status --fix first runs the remediations of unsatisfied checks. upgrade upgrades only auto dependencies and holds actively pinned ones unless --force. pin / unpin record holds in the user's ~/.config/vergil/host-pins.toml under the epic #155 pin-as-tech-debt doctrine. Runs unprivileged and refuses sudo/doas/su/pkexec. See the vrg-host reference.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_host Args status [--fix] (default); upgrade <dep>… or upgrade --all, each with optional --force; pin <dep> --constraint --inducing-release --reason [--tracking-issue] [--deterministic]; unpin <dep> Preconditions macOS host with each dependency installed by its documented method (Homebrew for the brew-formula and brew-cask entries, including uv) Failure mode Per-dependency probe-error rows (never fatal to the report); loud error on an unreadable manifest or pins file; refused pins and upgrades print the reason Exit codes status: 0 OK, 1 warnings, 2 errors; upgrade: 0 done, 1 a named dependency refused, 2 failure; pin/unpin: 0 success, 1 refused Status Active

docs.title: vrg-generate-commands
docs.text:
Generate MQSC command methods for all language ports (Python, Java, Go, Rust) from mapping-data.json. Updates target files between BEGIN/END GENERATED MQSC METHODS markers.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_generate_commands Args --language (required), --mapping-data (required), --target, --mapping-pages-dir, --check Preconditions mapping-data.json file exists at the given path Failure mode Explicit error for missing mapping data file Exit codes 0 success, 1 error or --check mismatch Status Active

docs.title: Container tools
docs.text: Container tools run inside dev containers launched by vrg-container-run. They assume language toolchain dependencies (ruff, mypy, shellcheck, markdownlint, yamllint) are available on PATH.

docs.title: vrg-validate
docs.text:
The unified validation driver. It reads [project].primary-language from vergil.toml and runs the stages in order: common checks, the language's install, lint, typecheck, test and audit commands, and last the repository's custom validator (scripts/bin/validate-custom or vrg-validate-custom on PATH) when it has one. --check runs one stage. --check custom runs the install stage (when the language has one) and then the custom stage; with no custom validator it prints one "no custom validator" line and exits 0, and a validator that is present but not an executable regular file fails. PR CI runs each stage through the vergil-actions reusable workflows, the custom stage as quality / custom. See the Validation Matrix for every check and where it runs.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_validate Args --check {common,lint,typecheck,test,audit,custom}, --all-versions (Python only; alone or with --check test) Preconditions Inside a dev container (run it as vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate) Failure mode Runs every stage after install and reports all failures in one run; install fails fast Exit codes 0 all passed, 1 a stage failed or the config is invalid, 2 usage error (for example --check custom --all-versions) Status Active

docs.title: vrg-validate-common
docs.text:
Shared validation checks for all repos: repository profile validation, markdownlint on published markdown (docs/site/**/*.md and README.md) using the bundled canonical config, shellcheck on scripts/, yamllint on .github/ and docs/ YAML files, the dependabot-limit guard (when .github/dependabot.yml exists, every updates entry must carry open-pull-requests-limit: 0, so Dependabot can never open a PR), hadolint on Dockerfile*, actionlint on .github/workflows/, and ansible-lint (using the bundled canonical config) when the repo carries Ansible content.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.validate_common Args None Preconditions Git repo, shellcheck and yamllint on PATH Failure mode Propagates exit codes from each tool Exit codes 0 all passed, non-zero on first failure Status Active (called internally by vrg-validate)

docs.title: vrg-repo-profile
docs.text:
Validate the repository configuration in vergil.toml (required keys, enum values, dependencies) and the README.md structure (exactly one H1, a Table of Contents, no heading-level skips). Run by vrg-validate as a common check. See the repo-profile reference.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_repo_profile Args None Preconditions Run from the repository root; vergil.toml exists Failure mode Exit 2 if vergil.toml is not found; exit 1 for an invalid vergil.toml or a README.md structure error Exit codes 0 valid, 1 invalid, 2 vergil.toml not found Status Active

docs.title: vrg-ci-resolve
docs.text:
Resolve the repo's CI versions from the published version window, with the same resolver vrg-validate and the dev container use. The CI setup step of the vergil-actions reusable workflows runs it to build the version matrix and pick the primary-version container. The window is read at the repo's [dependencies].vergil ref; set VRG_VERSION_WINDOW=<path> to resolve against a local window.json. A repo with no language resolves to latest. See Version resolution.

  • --format json (default) — one JSON object with versions, primary-version, primary-container-tag, container-tags and container-suffixes.
  • --format github-output — versions, primary-version and primary-container-tag as key=value lines for $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
  • --repo-root PATH — the directory holding vergil.toml (default: the current directory).
Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_ci_resolve Args --format {json,github-output}, --repo-root PATH Preconditions vergil.toml in the repo root; network access to the published window, or VRG_VERSION_WINDOW Failure mode vrg-ci-resolve: error: on stderr for a missing or invalid vergil.toml, an unreadable or malformed window, or a resolution error (a pin outside the window, an app pin of more than one version, a C++ or TypeScript repo with no pin) Exit codes 0 success, 1 error Status Active

docs.title: vrg-package
docs.text:
Build, install-test and index binary OS packages (.deb/.rpm) from the [package] section of vergil.toml in the current directory. Run by the ci-package, cd-release and publish-index reusable workflows; matrix is also useful locally. See the package config reference.

  • matrix — resolve [package] into build and test cells and print them as JSON (read-only). --tier {full,reduced} (default full), --github-output (append enabled/build/test/tier to $GITHUB_OUTPUT), --manifest PATH (also write the release artifact manifest). A repo without [package] reports enabled: false. Each python package resolves its runtime here, once, and records it as runtime on every build cell of that package and in the manifest's runtimes map. With several [[package]] entries, every cell id is qualified as <name>--<id>.
  • build — build every format of one build cell: --cell (required), --version (required), --out (default dist/packages), --staging (default .vergil/package-staging, wiped first), --runtime (the cell's recorded runtime; when empty or absent, the build resolves the runtime itself). Prints the runtime it chose. Needs nfpm on PATH.
  • check-runtime — refuse (exit 1) when any .deb/.rpm of a python package in --artifacts DIR does not depend on exactly the runtime that --manifest PATH records for that package. Read-only. See one runtime per package.
  • check-unpublished — refuse (exit 1) when a release at --version (required) would publish a package with the same name, full version, architecture and format as one an earlier stable release of --repo (default $GITHUB_REPOSITORY) already published. Read-only; needs gh. This is the CD backstop for the same check vrg-release runs in preflight. See the re-publish check.
  • install-test — in a clean container, install one test cell's artifact, verify shipped systemd units, run the smoke command and shim checks under a sanitized environment, remove the package and check for residue: --cell, --artifacts DIR, --report PATH (all required).
  • index — build the signed apt/dnf repository site: --config (packages.toml), --keys DIR, --out DIR (all required), --work (default .vergil/index-work), --base-url. Needs PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE.
Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_package Args Subcommand (matrix, build, check-runtime, check-unpublished, install-test, index) with the flags above Preconditions vergil.toml in the current directory (index: a packages.toml) Failure mode ERROR: diagnostic on stderr for config, package, or missing-file errors Exit codes 0 success, 1 error Status Active

docs.title: vrg-sarif-filter
docs.text:
Write a copy of a SARIF file with every accepted-suppressed result removed. The CI security composites upload the filtered copy to GitHub code scanning, while the CI-evidence bundle keeps the unfiltered original. See Suppressing a reviewed finding in source.

Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_sarif_filter Args INPUT OUTPUT (positional; may be the same path) Preconditions INPUT is a readable SARIF file Failure mode Error on stderr when the input cannot be read or the output cannot be written Exit codes 0 success, 1 error Status Active

docs.title: st-list-project-repos (removed)
docs.text: Entry point declared in pyproject.toml but the source module vergil_tooling.bin.list_project_repos did not exist. Would crash on import with ModuleNotFoundError. The underlying function (list_project_repos) lives in vergil_tooling.lib.github and is consumed by vrg-ensure-label --owner/--project mode.

docs.title: st-set-project-field (removed)
docs.text: Entry point declared in pyproject.toml but the source module vergil_tooling.bin.set_project_field did not exist. Would crash on import with ModuleNotFoundError.

docs.title: Precondition consistency
docs.text:
Most tools check preconditions explicitly and fail with clear messages. Notable gaps:

  • vrg-submit-pr does not validate that gh is on PATH before attempting git push and gh pr create. Failure surfaces as a subprocess error rather than a clear precondition message.
  • vrg-container-run checks GH_TOKEN explicitly; vrg-container-test does not (it will fail inside the container when gh commands run without a token, but the error is less clear).

docs.title: Args style
docs.text:
Most tools use argparse. Two exceptions:

  • vrg-container-run parses sys.argv manually with a -- separator.
  • vrg-container-docs parses sys.argv manually with subcommands.

Both are intentional: vrg-container-run passes everything after -- through to docker run, and vrg-container-docs has a simpler interface than argparse would provide. No alignment needed.

docs.title: Exit code contract
docs.text:
• 0: success
  • 1: check failure, validation error, or precondition violation
  • 2: infrastructure error (used by vrg-repo-profile)

The 1-vs-2 distinction is not universal. Tools added before the convention was established use 1 for all errors.

docs.title: GitHub Config Audit
docs.text:
vrg-github-repo-config audits a managed repo against the canonical Vergil configuration and, in apply mode, reconciles it. It combines two independent halves:

  • Local filesystem checks (audit_local_config) — pure local file I/O, no network. They verify the files every managed repo checks in: vergil.toml, CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/guard.sh, reusable-workflow pins, .gitignore, .github/dependabot.yml, and .github/workflows/ops.yml.
  • GitHub API checks — repo settings, branch rulesets, and the required-status-check set, fetched from the GitHub API.

docs.title: The audit command
docs.text:
vrg-github-repo-config audit [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--config PATH]
Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_github_repo_config Subcommands audit (report), diff (report GitHub half only), apply (reconcile GitHub half) Args --repo OWNER/REPO (defaults to the current git remote), --config PATH (local vergil.toml) Preconditions Local checks require running from inside the repo's own checkout; GitHub checks require gh credentials Exit codes 0 compliant, 1 non-compliant (drift), 2 audit could not complete Status Active

Local checks only run when the current directory is the audited repo's checkout — auditing a foreign --repo from elsewhere skips the local half with a warning rather than reading the wrong files.

docs.title: Where it runs — the nightly self-policing loop
docs.text:
The audit is not part of vrg-validate (that would add per-commit overhead for a check that only needs to catch slow drift). Its home is the nightly ops.yml config-audit job: every managed repo ships .github/workflows/ops.yml, which calls the reusable vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-github-config.yml workflow on a daily schedule. That job runs vrg-github-repo-config audit from inside the repo checkout, so any DiffItem returns exit 1 and turns the scheduled run red. Drift is fatal where it fires: a non-conforming repo cannot silently persist.

vrg-release also gates on the GitHub half of this audit, so a repo whose required-check set has drifted cannot release until reconciled.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
audit_local_config runs the following, appending a DiffItem for each divergence:

Check Asserts _check_vergil_toml vergil.toml present and parseable _check_hook_guard_shim .claude/hooks/guard.sh present _check_claude_md CLAUDE.md carries the canonical consumer template verbatim _check_claude_settings .claude/settings.json marketplace, enabledPlugins and attribution match the template _check_workflow_refs every vergil-* reusable-workflow pin matches the vergil.toml version _check_gitignore .gitignore carries the correct base + <language> vergil-managed fence (#311, #325) _check_dependabot_yml .github/dependabot.yml is the canonical report-only render for the repo's language (.github#420) _check_required_workflows ops.yml is present, wires the audit, and is scheduled (new, #311)

docs.title: _check_claude_settings — attribution
docs.text:
.claude/settings.json must carry exactly:

"attribution": { "commit": "", "pr": "" }

This turns off Claude Code's AI Co-Authored-By trailer on commits and PRs; AI co-author attribution is not used (#3200). The empty-string form is required: attribution: false needs a newer Claude Code and makes older versions skip the whole settings file. A missing or different value is a hard failure, DiffItem(field="local.claude_settings.attribution", ...), whose expected value names the key and #3200. Fix it by adding the block above to the repo's checked-in .claude/settings.json.

The check was warning-only while the fleet was swept and became strict in #3361. There is no exemption for dormant repos: a dormant repo whose nightly audit still runs fails until the key is added. Each dormant repo carries a backlog issue to add the key when it is revived.

docs.title: _check_gitignore — managed fence
docs.text:
The repo's .gitignore must carry the vergil-managed fence for its resolved language (see The composed managed fence). The check is fenced-only: a well-formed fence must be present, its body must equal render_block(<language>) exactly, and no managed-vocabulary pattern may appear loose outside the fence. Each failed condition is reported as DiffItem(field="local.gitignore", expected="vergil-managed fence", actual=<reason>); a repo with no .gitignore fails because no fence is present. Genuinely repo-local lines outside the fence are never asserted against.

The resolved language is [project].primary-language. No vergil.toml, or no declared language, means base-only. A vergil.toml that fails to load is not treated as base-only: the fence cannot be judged, so the check reports one explicit failure, DiffItem(field="local.gitignore", expected="resolvable [project].primary-language", actual="cannot resolve the fence language: <config error>"), and nothing else for the file (#3451).

The resolved language is the repo's [project].primary-language, normalized to base-only for any language without a managed fragment — the same rule scaffolding uses, so a freshly inited repo is fenced-compliant by construction. The transitional legacy monolith-superset acceptance was removed in epic #325, Task 10.

docs.title: _check_dependabot_yml — report-only Dependabot config
docs.text:
The repo's .github/dependabot.yml must be exactly the canonical report-only render for its [project].primary-language (epic vergil-project/.github#420): a github-actions entry plus the language's ecosystem, each with open-pull-requests-limit: 0. The comparison is an exact match with no local additions — the same lib/dependabot.py::check that vrg-dependabot-sync --check uses. Each failure is reported as DiffItem(field="local.dependabot", expected="canonical report-only dependabot.yml", actual=<reason>), where the reason is missing .github/dependabot.yml or differs from the canonical render. Fix either with vrg-dependabot-sync --write.

No vergil.toml, or no declared language, means the actions-only render. A vergil.toml that fails to load is not treated as actions-only: the check reports one explicit failure, DiffItem(field="local.dependabot", expected="resolvable [project].primary-language", actual="cannot resolve the dependabot language: <config error>"), and nothing else for the file (#3451).

docs.title: _check_required_workflows — ops.yml wiring
docs.text:
A wiring validator for a present ops.yml. It asserts the file (a) exists, (b) references ops-github-config.yml (so a repo cannot carry an ops.yml that omits the config audit), and (c) carries a scheduled (cron) trigger — because a wired-but-unscheduled ops.yml (e.g. workflow_dispatch only) would pass a bare wiring check yet never run nightly, silently defeating the self-policing mechanism.

Structural limit — a missing ops.yml is not caught here

Because this check runs inside the nightly ops.yml job, it cannot detect a repo that lacks ops.yml entirely — such a repo has no nightly run, so nothing executes the check there. The local validator keeps a present ops.yml honest; guaranteeing presence across the fleet needs a from-outside auditor, deferred to follow-on C (#315). In the meantime, presence is established by repo_init scaffolding (new repos) and the one-time rollout (existing repos).

docs.title: The composed managed fence
docs.text:
The source of truth for the fleet's ignore vocabulary is a set of packaged data-asset fragments:

src/vergil_tooling/data/gitignore/base        # language-agnostic
src/vergil_tooling/data/gitignore/<language>  # one per managed language

They are loaded at runtime via importlib.resources — the same idiom used for the CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json templates — and lib/gitignore.py composes base + <language> into an order-stable, de-duplicated pattern list. Scaffolding, the applicator (vrg-gitignore-sync), and the audit all render through that one module, so they cannot diverge.

Composed per language. A repo's block is the union of the language-agnostic base (editors, OS, secrets, logs, Vergil internals like .venv/ / .worktrees/ / .vergil/ / .superpowers/, paad's paad/security/ output, and all build/validation/CI-evidence output including the mkdocs build path docs/site/site/ and the paths vrg-container-docs stages: docs/site/docs/changelog.md, docs/site/docs/releases/ and mkdocs.staged.yml) plus the fragment for its [project].primary-language (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, C++; Rust and Java are managed with an empty fragment). A repo that declares no fragment language gets the base-only block.

The managed fence. The composed block is written into .gitignore between a # >>> vergil-managed: base + <language> … begin marker and a # <<< vergil-managed <<< end marker. The audit (lib/gitignore.py::check) is fenced-only: it requires a well-formed fence whose body equals the composed block for the repo's language exactly, with no managed pattern left loose outside the fence, in the exact layout vrg-gitignore-sync --write produces: the fence first and a trailing newline, so the audit drifts exactly when --write would change the file (#3568). (The transitional legacy monolith-superset acceptance and the monolithic gitignore.baseline asset were removed in epic #325, Task 10, once the whole fleet was fenced.)

Local additions are expected. Genuinely repo-local lines live outside the fence and are never asserted against; a repo freely adds its own entries below the managed block (--write moves any above it to below it, in order).

docs.title: Propagation — the rolling vX.Y pin
docs.text:
Every managed repo pins vergil-tooling to the rolling major-minor tag vX.Y, never a specific patch. The nightly ops.yml job installs vergil-tooling@vX.Y, which always resolves to the latest patch under that line — including its fragment set. So:

change a fragment → release a vergil-tooling patch under vX.Y → every repo's nightly audit flags the fence as drifted until its managed block is re-rendered.

Because the fence must match the composed block exactly (not merely be a superset), a fragment change is applied — not auto-satisfied — by re-running vrg-gitignore-sync, which rewrites the managed block in place and leaves the genuinely repo-local section untouched. The fleet driver runs that applicator across every repo as reviewed per-repo PRs; the rolling pin delivers the new fragments to the tool, and the applicator writes the fence.

docs.title: New repos are born conforming
docs.text:
repo_init (vrg-github-repo-init) scaffolds these checked-in files through the same modules the audit uses, so a freshly created repo passes their checks from day one:

  • .gitignore — render_gitignore() renders through lib/gitignore.py (the same module the audit uses), so a new repo is born with a correct base + <language> managed fence and passes the fenced-only audit by construction.
  • ops.yml — render_ops_workflow() writes .github/workflows/ops.yml calling ops-github-config.yml@vX.Y on a daily schedule. The scheduled minute is staggered per repo — a deterministic hash of <org>/<repo> maps to a minute in [0,59] — so the fleet does not stampede a single minute as it grows. The hour stays in the early-UTC window; only the minute varies.
  • .github/dependabot.yml — the config-files step writes lib/dependabot.py::render(<language>), the same render _check_dependabot_yml compares against, so a new repo passes that check from day one.

docs.title: GitHub checks — security settings
docs.text:
The GitHub half also compares the repo's security settings (desired_security_settings() in lib/github_config.py) and reports each difference as a security.<field> DiffItem:

Field Desired Notes security.vulnerability_alerts true Dependabot alerts on, for every repo, public or private security.dependabot_security_updates disabled Dependabot never opens a security-update PR security.secret_scanning enabled Only when GHAS is available; otherwise unmanaged security.secret_scanning_push_protection enabled Only when GHAS is available; otherwise unmanaged

GHAS is available when [project].ghas in vergil.toml says so, and otherwise exactly when the repo is not private.

The first two rows are the report-only Dependabot posture (epic vergil-project/.github#420): alerts are on so the nightly vrg-dependabot-audit has something to read, and security-update PRs stay off. Version-update PRs are suppressed separately, by open-pull-requests-limit: 0 in the canonical .github/dependabot.yml, which _check_dependabot_yml enforces (see Local checks).

Alerts are read from GET /repos/{repo}/vulnerability-alerts (204 means on, 404 means off). Any other status is an error, never a silent "off". apply turns alerts on with PUT on that endpoint (or off with DELETE), and sets dependabot_security_updates through the repo's security_and_analysis settings. apply is a human action: it needs Administration write access, which the org automation Apps do not have.

docs.title: GitHub checks — the required-status-check set
docs.text:
The GitHub half compares the repo's live branch-protection configuration against the canonical CI-gates ruleset that desired_ci_gates_ruleset() computes from vergil.toml. Three properties matter for the dynamic, version-agnostic CI model (epic vergil-project/.github#338):

  • Version-agnostic required checks. For the matrixed kinds the desired set requires the stable audit / evidence, quality / evidence, and test / evidence aggregates — never per-version legs such as audit / dependencies / 3.12. A [ci].versions change no longer churns the required-check set, so the ruleset stops drifting when the matrix changes. A repo with a [package] section additionally requires package / evidence, the single aggregate over its binary-package target matrix.
  • Unproducible-context check. The audit asserts every required context is one the repo's workflows can actually produce. A leftover required leg that no workflow emits — for example a stale per-version check surviving a matrix reduction — is reported as drift rather than silently sitting "expected, never reported" and blocking every PR.
  • Apply-time producibility guard. Before apply writes anything, it fetches the repo's committed .github/workflows/ci.yml from develop and refuses (exit 1) if the desired CI gates ruleset requires a context no pull_request job in that file emits — the same guard repo-init runs against the ci.yml it generates. A missing ci.yml is also a refusal, never a skip: with no workflow, no required check could ever report.
  • Classic branch-protection read + scoped cleanup. The audit reads legacy classic branch protection in addition to the rulesets API. When it reconciles, it removes only the stale version-suffixed CI contexts the evidence ruleset now owns; every other classic setting (review requirements, push restrictions) is reported, not touched. The blast radius is minimal and intentional protections are preserved.

docs.title: GitHub checks — undeclared ruleset parameters
docs.text:
GitHub sometimes adds a new ruleset rule parameter and sets a default for it on its side, as it did with require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes on the pull_request rule (#2860). When a live rule carries a parameter key that the desired rule of the same type does not declare, the audit reports it as an undeclared parameter, separately from value mismatches. The message names the ruleset, the rule type, the key, and the live value:

UNDECLARED PARAMETER: rulesets.Branch protection rule 'pull_request' has
'require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes' = True live, ...
  • It is non-compliant. The live ruleset enforces a setting the spec never chose, so audit exits 1, the same as any other drift.
  • apply cannot fix it. The ruleset PUT leaves out the key, so GitHub applies its default again. apply still fixes any value drift, writes nothing when the only issues are undeclared parameters, and exits 1 with a pointer to the decision.
  • Resolve it in the spec. Either declare the key with an explicit value in the desired ruleset in lib/github_config.py, or add it to _STRIP_RULE_PARAMS if it should be ignored. Keys on that list (do_not_enforce_on_create, dismissal_restriction) are removed before comparison and never reported.

A whole live rule whose type the desired ruleset lacks is not an undeclared parameter. It is reported as .rules value drift.

docs.title: Container Config Reference ([container])
docs.text:
A repo customizes its dev container through the [container] section of its vergil.toml. The section is optional; every key defaults to empty, so a repo that omits [container] behaves exactly as it would with an empty table.

The keys describe the same container from a few angles: env-prefixes controls which host environment variables vrg-container-run forwards into the container, system-packages declares Debian packages installed inside it, and build-command runs a repo-declared provisioning step when the cached dev image is built (with build-cache-files naming the inputs that invalidate the cache).

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
[container]
env-prefixes = ["MQ_"]                          # forward matching host env vars
system-packages = ["lilypond"]                  # install Debian packages
build-command = "npm install -g @coderline/alphatab"  # provision non-apt deps
build-cache-files = ["package-lock.json"]       # inputs that invalidate the cache

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Default Semantics env-prefixes list of strings [] Host env-var name prefixes vrg-container-run forwards into the container (accumulates) system-packages list of strings [] Debian apt package names baked into the local cached dev image and installed on CI test jobs (see below) build-command string (unset) A shell command run while the cached dev image is built, to provision a non-apt dependency outside /workspace (see below) build-cache-files list of strings [] Repo-relative files the build-command reads; folded into the image cache hash so a bump forces a rebuild

docs.title: env-prefixes
docs.text:
Each entry is a prefix; any host environment variable whose name starts with it is passed through when vrg-container-run launches the container. This is how a consuming repo gets a secret or token — held only in the host environment — into the container without hard-coding its name in tooling.

The ConanCenter audit token does not need an env-prefixes entry. For a cpp repo, vrg-container-run resolves it from the environment or its canonical token file and forwards it itself (see the next section and C++ Overview → ConanCenter Audit Token). An existing CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN prefix is harmless but redundant. The passthrough design is specified in docs/specs/2026-05-25-configurable-container-env-passthrough-design.md.

docs.title: Variables vrg-container-run always sets
docs.text:
Besides the forwarded variables, every container launch sets a few itself. Each is emitted after the env-prefixes passthrough, and the container runtime applies the last -e given for a name, so a matching prefix cannot override the value vrg-container-run resolves:

Variable Default Host override UV_LINK_MODE copy (the uv cache and /workspace are on different filesystems) An explicit host value wins PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX /tmp/pycache (container-local, discarded with the container) A non-empty host value wins; an empty value falls back to the default NODE_PATH npm global root, only when build-command is declared (see below) An explicit host value wins UV_PYTHON, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE Python only: the resolved primary version and only-system None: the resolver decides

For a Python repo, UV_PYTHON and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system make uv use the image's interpreter at the resolved version, so a repo's own python-preference cannot make uv download a managed interpreter. The cached-image build exports the same two variables for its whole setup step (vergil-tooling install, build-command and warmup), and they are part of the image's cache key, so a change of resolved version rebuilds the image (#3421). vrg-container-docs resolves no version, so for a Python repo it sets only UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system, which pins uv to the docs image's own Python, as the CI docs jobs do. If that Python does not satisfy requires-python, uv fails the build; there is no fallback (#3414).

For a cpp repo, vrg-container-run also forwards CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER when it can resolve one: from the environment if set and not blank, else from ~/.config/vergil/conan.env, else from the conan_audit_token_path file in ~/.config/vergil/identities.toml. The value goes to the container runtime through its environment, never its command line. A token source that exists but is unreadable or malformed stops the run with an error, and with no token at all nothing is forwarded (see C++ Overview → ConanCenter Audit Token).

PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX keeps Python bytecode (including pytest's rewritten test modules) out of the bind-mounted repo. Parallel test workers writing __pycache__ over the macOS-to-container mount could leave a truncated .pyc that a later run trusted, failing with EOFError: marshal data too short on code that was fine (#3111). With the prefix, bytecode is still cached and shared by every worker within a run, and any stale .pyc already in the working tree is ignored. A host override pointing inside the repo would put bytecode back on the mount, so keep any override outside it.

docs.title: VRG_VERSION_WINDOW: a local version window
docs.text:
The version resolver reads the language version window that vergil-containers publishes at the repo's [dependencies].vergil ref, over the network. VRG_VERSION_WINDOW=<path> is the one sanctioned override: it names a local window.json to resolve from instead, for example to validate offline. The published window is never silently replaced, and an explicit override is never silently dropped (epic vergil-project/.github#407).

A host path is not visible inside the container, so vrg-container-run does not forward the variable as is. When VRG_VERSION_WINDOW is set on the host, it:

  1. resolves the path to an absolute one (a relative path is taken from the current directory);
  2. stops on the host, before any image work, if the value is empty, the path is not an existing file, or the path contains a : (which the -v bind syntax cannot carry). The error names the path;
  3. bind-mounts the file read-only at /run/vergil/version-window.json;
  4. sets VRG_VERSION_WINDOW=/run/vergil/version-window.json in the container.

The run banner shows the file in use (Window: <path> (VRG_VERSION_WINDOW)). The host value is never forwarded, even when an env-prefixes entry such as VRG_ matches it. When the variable is unset, nothing changes: the container fetches the published window.

VRG_VERSION_WINDOW=/abs/path/window.json vrg-container-run -- vrg-ci-resolve

docs.title: system-packages
docs.text:
A list of Debian package names — nothing more. Vergil's container model otherwise treats a system dependency as a property of the language (dev-python:3.14 means the same thing everywhere), which is what makes the per-branch image cache sound. system-packages is the sanctioned escape hatch for the case where one repo genuinely needs a binary that is not a language package — for example a repo whose tests shell out to the LilyPond renderer (apt-get install lilypond) — without adding anything repo-specific to the shared base images (epic vergil-project/.github#272).

The packages are installed with:

apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends <names>

from the base image's existing apt sources (Debian main). The surface is deliberately narrow — names only:

  • No third-party apt sources, signing keys, add-apt-repository, or install scripts.
  • No version pins, build flags, or post-install steps.

docs.title: Where the packages take effect
docs.text:
The same declaration is applied by two different paths, which agree on what is installed while differing on when:

  • Locally the packages are baked into the per-branch cached dev image that vrg-container-run builds over the base (container_cache.py), so they are present for every check in that one image.
  • In CI they are installed by a composite setup step only on the jobs that run the repo's own tests — never on lint or typecheck (composite action added in vergil-actions#807).

Test-runtime contract. A declared system package is a test-runtime dependency. Because it is test-only in CI, repos must not rely on a system package during lint or typecheck. The local one-image convenience (visible to every check) does not license depending on it outside test jobs; the divergence is deliberate, sound because these binaries are genuinely needed only at test time. See CI Architecture → Repo-specific system packages for the mechanism in full.

docs.title: Fail-closed on the build architecture
docs.text:
The cache layer builds on the host architecture (Apple Silicon → linux/arm64; the CI runner's arch). If a declared package has no installation candidate for that architecture, the build and the CI setup step both fail immediately, naming the package and the architecture:

system package 'X' is not installable on linux/arm64 (apt: no installation candidate)

There is no silent skip and no degraded image — a missing dependency stops the build rather than producing a container that fails mysteriously inside a test.

docs.title: Cache key
docs.text: vergil.toml is already part of the cache-sensitive file set, so editing system-packages changes the per-branch image's cache hash and forces a rebuild. No special-casing is needed, and an empty or absent list is byte-identical to a repo that declares no packages at all.

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text: A repo can express Debian package names only, installed from the base image's existing sources, as root — exactly what the base image already grants. It cannot fetch arbitrary URLs or run arbitrary code. Adding to system-packages is a vergil.toml change reviewed like any config change, via the PR diff: the list is a plain, greppable set of names. There is no separate allowlist — the constrained surface plus the fail-closed build is the backstop for typos and nonexistent names.

docs.title: Inspecting the declared list
docs.text:
vrg-container-system-packages reads the key through the same single accessor the local bake and CI both use (container_system_packages in config.py):

vrg-container-system-packages                   # the declared names, one per line
vrg-container-system-packages --install-script  # the exact apt snippet CI runs

The plain-list mode is a human-facing inspection affordance ("what would this repo install?"); --install-script emits the single, shared apt speller that both the local image build and the CI step execute verbatim.

docs.title: build-command
docs.text: A shell command run once while the per-branch cached dev image is built (after the system-packages apt step and the vergil-tooling install, before the language warmup). It is the escape hatch for a dependency that is not an apt package and not a language package the base image already carries — for example a JS library a test driver consumes at runtime (epic vergil-project/.github#291).

docs.title: The out-of-workspace contract
docs.text:
vrg-container-run bind-mounts the repo over /workspace at run time, which masks anything the build wrote under /workspace. So a build-command must install its artifact outside /workspace (a global/system location baked into the image), or the run-time mount hides it. A global install is the usual way to land outside the workspace — e.g. npm install -g <pkg> writes to /usr/lib/node_modules, which is image-resident and survives the mount.

Landing the artifact outside /workspace makes it present, but present is not the same as resolvable, and the two differ by artifact kind:

  • Executables are on PATH. A globally-installed CLI (npm install -g of a package with a bin, a pip install console script, a Go binary in /usr/local/bin) is on PATH and runs as-is — no extra configuration.
  • Libraries are not automatically on the language's module-resolution path. This is the correction to the earlier contract wording: a global npm install -g of a library is not "on the default resolution path." A global npm install puts executables on PATH but does not add the npm global root (/usr/lib/node_modules) to Node's require search path. Without help, require("<lib>") / require.resolve("<lib>") returns MODULE_NOT_FOUND even though the package is baked into the image (validated in vergil-project/vergil-tooling#2766; this also corrects the design spec's §4, tracked for the epic doc-sweep #2756).

docs.title: NODE_PATH for baked npm libraries
docs.text:
To make a baked npm library resolvable, vrg-container-run sets NODE_PATH to the npm global root (/usr/lib/node_modules, i.e. npm root -g on the vergil base images) whenever the repo declares a build-command, so require.resolve("<lib>") resolves out of the box. A repo that declares no build-command is unaffected — no NODE_PATH is set, and its container environment is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Two caveats:

  • CommonJS only. NODE_PATH is honoured by CommonJS require; ESM import ignores it. A library consumed via ESM import needs a different mechanism (e.g. a repo-local node_modules populated by npm ci, or staging the module into a directory ESM resolution walks up to).
  • Overridable. An explicit NODE_PATH in the host environment wins, so a consumer can point resolution at a different location at run time.

The value rides the container run invocation rather than being baked into the image with commit --change ENV, because the nerdctl runtime's commit --change supports only CMD/ENTRYPOINT directives (not ENV); setting it on the run path works identically across the docker and nerdctl runtimes.

docs.title: Cache key
docs.text: Like system-packages, editing build-command changes vergil.toml, which is in the cache-sensitive file set, so a change forces an image rebuild. When the command reads a lockfile whose contents (not the command string) determine what gets installed, list that lockfile in build-cache-files so a dependency bump also invalidates the cache.

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text:
build-command is a deliberate broadening of the surface system-packages grants. Where system-packages is names-only — Debian packages installed from the base image's existing sources, with no allowlist because the surface is already constrained — build-command is arbitrary shell, run as root, at image-build time. It can fetch URLs, run installers, and write anywhere in the image. That is the point (it is the escape hatch for a dependency apt cannot express), and it is what makes it a larger grant.

The controls that keep it sound:

  • Reviewed via the vergil.toml PR diff. The command is a plain string in the repo's own vergil.toml; adding or changing it is a config change read and approved like any other in the PR diff. There is no separate allowlist (unlike the names-only system-packages surface, none is needed) — the diff is the review surface.
  • The fail-closed build is the backstop. The command runs while the cached image is built; a non-zero exit fails the build rather than producing a degraded image, exactly as the system-packages apt step does. A broken provisioning step stops the build, it does not leak into a mysteriously failing test.
  • Artifacts are image-resident and out-of-workspace. Whatever the command installs lands in the image outside /workspace (see the out-of-workspace contract above); it never writes into the mounted repo tree at run time.
  • No build-time network secrets by default. The build step runs with the image build's environment, not the run-time forward set — a build-command sees a host secret only if the repo deliberately forwards it. Keep credentials out of the command string, which is stored in vergil.toml verbatim.

docs.title: Inspecting the declared command
docs.text:
vrg-container-build-command reads the key through the same single accessor the local bake and CI both use (container_build_command in config.py):

vrg-container-build-command            # the declared command (nothing if unset)
vrg-container-build-command --script   # the same command, emitted for CI to run

Both modes print the command verbatim; a repo that declares no build-command prints nothing. --script is the CI-consumption entry point — the CI test jobs call it to obtain the exact command to run per job (see CI Architecture → Repo-specific build steps), mirroring how vrg-container-system-packages --install-script feeds the apt step.

docs.title: Low-disk auto-prune (VRG_CACHE_PRUNE_FREE_GB, VRG_CACHE_BUILD_FREE_GB)
docs.text:
Not [container] keys: the image store belongs to the machine, not the repo, so these are host environment variables.

Just before vrg-container-run (or vrg-container-cache build, or vrg-finalize-pr's provisioning step) builds a cached dev image, it checks the free space on the filesystem that holds the runtime's image store. When that is below the threshold, it runs the same prune as vrg-container-cache prune --apply against the same repo set, and prints each image it removed.

Variable Default Semantics VRG_CACHE_PRUNE_FREE_GB 10 Free space, in GB, below which a cache build first prunes finished branches' images. 0 turns the auto-prune off; a value that is not a non-negative number stops the build VRG_CACHE_BUILD_FREE_GB 3 Free space, in GB, a cache build needs after the prune to go ahead at all (one cached image is about 1.3–2 GB). Capped at VRG_CACHE_PRUNE_FREE_GB: when the threshold is lower, the threshold is the floor. 0 lets the build go ahead whatever is left; a value that is not a non-negative number stops the build
  • The repo set is never guessed. On the physical host, which has no default repo set, the prune is skipped with a warning; run vrg-container-cache prune --apply --root DIR by hand.
  • Failures are loud. A prune that cannot run, or an image it cannot remove, is printed as a warning.
  • The build goes ahead only with room for it. After the prune, the build continues if at least VRG_CACHE_BUILD_FREE_GB (default 3 GB; or the threshold, if lower) is free, with a warning while still below the threshold. With less, it stops with the free-space numbers, the setting that set the floor, and the manual command, rather than fail part way through.
  • A bad value is never ignored. Both variables are read before every cache build, so a value that is not a non-negative number stops the build with an error naming the variable, even when the disk has room — never a silent fallback to the default.
  • An unmeasurable store is skipped. Docker Desktop keeps its image store inside its own VM; there the check is skipped with a note.

docs.title: Dependabot Alert Audit
docs.text:
vrg-dependabot-audit fails when a repository has any open Dependabot alert. It is the gate for the fleet's report-only Dependabot posture (epic vergil-project/.github#420). Dependabot alerts are on for every managed repo, Dependabot never opens a pull request, and this command turns an open alert into a failing run.

vrg-dependabot-audit --repo OWNER/REPO
Attribute Value Source vergil_tooling.bin.vrg_dependabot_audit Args --repo OWNER/REPO (required) Preconditions A GitHub token that can read the repo's Dependabot alerts (see Required permission) Exit codes 0 no open alerts, 1 at least one open alert, 2 could not check Status Active

docs.title: The report-only posture
docs.text:
Two halves keep Dependabot to reporting:

  • Alerts are on. vrg-github-repo-config apply enables vulnerability alerts on every repo, public or private, and the nightly config audit flags any repo where they are off.
  • Dependabot never opens a PR. The repo setting for Dependabot security updates stays disabled, which the config audit also enforces. Version-update PRs are suppressed by the canonical .github/dependabot.yml, where every updates entry carries open-pull-requests-limit: 0. vrg-validate rejects any entry without it, and the nightly config audit's local.dependabot check flags a missing or non-canonical file. vrg-dependabot-sync writes the file for one repo, and vrg-fleet-sync --target dependabot sweeps it across the fleet. See the GitHub Config Audit reference and the CLI Tools Overview.

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text:
Every managed repo's nightly ops.yml calls the reusable vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-github-config.yml workflow. Its dependabot-audit job runs vrg-dependabot-audit --repo "${{ github.repository }}", so exit 1 or exit 2 turns the scheduled run red, and GitHub's failed-workflow notification is the alert.

The job cannot use GITHUB_TOKEN: a called workflow gets only what the caller's ops.yml grants, which is contents: read. It mints a token from the org's automation App (the APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets), scoped to the calling repo and carrying only vulnerability-alerts: read. See Identity Architecture.

The audit reads only alerts in the open state, across every page of the API result, so a repo with hundreds of alerts is counted in full.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 The repo has no open Dependabot alerts. 1 The repo has at least one open alert, at any severity. 2 The audit could not read the alerts.

There is no severity threshold and no in-repo suppression. A low severity alert fails the audit exactly as a critical one does.

Exit 2 is never a pass. The command prints one diagnostic line to stderr, prefixed vrg-dependabot-audit:. The common causes are:

Diagnostic Cause Dependabot alerts are disabled for OWNER/REPO Alerts are off on the repo. Run vrg-github-repo-config apply. token lacks the 'Dependabot alerts: Read' permission for OWNER/REPO The token or GitHub App cannot read alerts (HTTP 403). repository OWNER/REPO not found or not accessible The repo does not exist or the token cannot see it (HTTP 404). the GitHub App has no installation for owner '…' No App installation for the repo's owner. could not read Dependabot alerts for OWNER/REPO: … Any other API failure; the first line of the error follows.

docs.title: Output: public vs private repos
docs.text:
Every report starts with a totals line, then ends with a link to the repo's Security tab:

o/r: 2 open Dependabot alerts: 1 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, 1 low
Review or dismiss at https://github.com/o/r/security/dependabot

A severity GitHub adds beyond the four known ones is still counted, and it is listed after low.

  • Private repos also get one line per alert, ordered by severity and then package. Each line carries the severity, ecosystem, package, manifest path, GHSA ID, and the alert's URL.
  • Public repos get the totals line and the link only. Package names, manifest paths, and GHSA IDs never appear, because the log of a public repo's workflow run is world-readable. An internal repo is treated like a public one.

If the repo's visibility cannot be resolved, the command warns on stderr and uses the public, counts-only format. It never itemizes a repo it has not confirmed is private.

docs.title: Clearing an alert
docs.text: Dismissal on GitHub is the only escape hatch. Fix the dependency, or dismiss the alert from the Security tab with a reason. Because the audit reads only open alerts, a fixed or dismissed alert no longer fails it. There is no file or setting in the repo that suppresses an alert.

docs.title: Required permission
docs.text:
The token needs read access to Dependabot alerts:

  • GitHub App: the Dependabot alerts: Read repository permission, and each installation must accept the updated permission.
  • Personal access token: the fine-grained Dependabot alerts: Read permission, or the classic security_events scope (or public_repo for a public repo).

As with vrg-github-repo-config, when the command mints its own GitHub App token it mints it for the audited repo's owner, not for the current directory's remote.

docs.title: Dependency Update Reference ([dependency-update])
docs.text:
Every vrg-release ends with an update-deps stage that updates the repo's dependencies to the newest versions their declared bounds allow (see Dependency updates). vrg-update-deps runs the same pipeline by hand. This page covers what that pipeline updates: the built-in updaters, the per-repo hook a repo configures with [dependency-update] in vergil.toml, and the held-back report.

The design is epic vergil-project/.github#381 (spec epics/381-release-dep-updates/spec.md).

docs.title: Updaters
docs.text:
The updaters run in this order. Each one runs only when the repo has what it updates, and each one's changes become a separate commit on the deps/update-<version> branch.

Name Runs when Commit message python pyproject.toml and uv.lock exist chore(deps): uv lock --upgrade vergil vergil.toml exists chore(deps): … naming what changed images A Dockerfile, workflow or action.yml is tracked chore(deps): bump image tags hook [dependency-update].hook is set chore(deps): repo hook

Bounds are always the repo's own: a dependency is never moved past what its manifest allows. Anything newer than the bounds allow is reported in the held-back report instead. Third-party GitHub Actions are not updated. A registry or index lookup that fails is an error, never "nothing to update".

docs.title: python
docs.text:
Runs uv lock --upgrade in the dev container, which refreshes uv.lock within the ranges pyproject.toml declares.

It then compares every directly declared requirement with its latest release on PyPI. The direct requirements are those in [project] dependencies, every dependency group, [build-system] requires and [tool.uv] constraint-dependencies. A requirement whose latest release falls outside its own specifier is reported as held back. Requirements without a specifier, URL requirements and transitive packages are never reported.

docs.title: vergil
docs.text:
Keeps the vergil ecosystem references consistent with [dependencies].vergil in vergil.toml:

  • Rewrites drifting uses: vergil-*/…@vX.Y refs in .github/workflows/ and in every action.yml/action.yaml in the repo.
  • Sets the vergil marketplace source.ref in .claude/settings.json to main.
  • With vrg-update-deps --vergil X.Y, first sets [dependencies].vergil to vX.Y, then rewrites the refs to match.

For a repo with an exact [package.python] runtime pin such as 3.14.8 (see Package Config), it also bumps the pin to the CPython patch that the pin's series package, vergil-python3.14, serves. That package's version is <cpython>+<pbs_tag>.<release> (for example 3.14.9+20261021.1.0.4, where 1.0.4 is the vergil-python release; releases before v1.0.4 have no .<release> suffix), and the patch is the part before the +. Each index installs the newest version it lists, and the patch counts only when every apt and rpm index the package build and install test read from serves the same one, so the bump cannot pass validation and then break the next release.

The pin never leaves its series. A newer series, such as vergil-python3.15, is reported as held back and never applied; moving to it is a reviewed change.

The deb and rpm indexes publish separately, so right after a vergil-python release they can briefly serve different patches. While they disagree the pin is left unchanged and the held-back report names each patch and the indexes serving it, for example indexes disagree (3.14.9 on deb noble/amd64; 3.14.8 on rpm el9/x86_64); bump held until they agree. A later run bumps the pin once they agree.

The update fails loudly, rather than reporting "no change", when:

  • any of those indexes lacks the series package, or cannot be read. The legacy per-patch packages (vergil-python3.14.8) are retired and are not read;
  • a series package version is not <cpython>+<pbs_tag>, optionally followed by .<release>;
  • the series package serves a patch on another series, or a patch older than the pin.

docs.title: images
docs.text:
Updates container image tags in Dockerfile FROM lines, workflow container: and image: values, and the defaults of action.yml inputs whose names end in image. Tags are looked up anonymously in the image's registry.

Tag shape Example What happens Exact x.y.z (optional v prefix) 0.71.0, v1.2.3 Bumped to the newest tag with the same major. A newer major is reported, never bumped Numeric series 3.14-slim, 24.04, 16 Never bumped. A newer series with the same suffix is reported latest, digests, expressions ${{ inputs.image }}, $BASE Skipped ghcr.io/vergil-project/* Skipped Anything else trixie-slim Skipped

Toolchain and language majors are therefore only ever reported.

docs.title: hook
docs.text: The per-repo hook, configured below. It always runs last, so it sees the lockfiles the built-in updaters have already refreshed.

docs.title: [dependency-update]
docs.text:
[dependency-update]
hook = "scripts/dev/update-deps.sh"
Key Type Default Semantics hook string (required) Command to run after the built-in updaters. Must be non-empty

The table is optional; without it, no hook runs. When the table is present, hook is required. hook is the only key; any other key is reported as an unrecognised-key warning.

Use the hook for what the built-in updaters do not cover, such as binary tool versions or provider pins. Keep repo-specific update logic in the repo, not in vergil-tooling.

This hook is separate from the [upstream-refresh] hook: vrg-update-deps never runs the upstream-refresh hook, and vrg-upstream-refresh never runs this one.

docs.title: The hook contract
docs.text:
The hook runs from the root of the update worktree, inside the dev container:

vrg-container-run -- env VRG_DEPS_REPORT=/workspace/.vergil/deps-report.jsonl <hook>

The hook string is split into words the way a shell would, but it is not run through a shell. To use pipes, && or other shell syntax, put them in a script and point hook at the script.

  • Edit files; do not commit. The driver commits the hook's changes as chore(deps): repo hook. If the hook moves HEAD, the update fails.
  • Exit 0 on success. A non-zero exit fails the update. It is never treated as "nothing to update".
  • Report what you hold back by appending lines to $VRG_DEPS_REPORT (see below). The file starts empty on each run.

A hook failure is an update failure: nothing is pushed and no PR is opened, but a fix task naming the hook is filed.

docs.title: The held-back report
docs.text:
The held-back report lists the dependencies whose newest release is outside the bounds the repo declares. It appears in the dependency-update PR body, in the update-deps comment on the release tracking issue, and at the end of every vrg-update-deps run, as a table:

Source Dependency Current Latest Note python example-lib 1.4.2 2.0.0 project.dependencies: example-lib<2

When nothing is held back it says "No dependencies are held back by their declared bounds."

A hook adds entries by writing one JSON object per line to $VRG_DEPS_REPORT:

{"source": "tofu", "name": "hashicorp/aws", "current": "5.80.0", "latest": "6.2.0", "note": "provider pinned to ~> 5.0"}
Key Required Type source Yes string name Yes string current Yes string latest Yes string note No string

Blank lines are ignored. Every other line must be a JSON object that has all the required keys, no other keys, and only string values. A malformed line fails the update, and the error names the line number.

docs.title: Package Config Reference ([package])
docs.text:
A repo publishes its product as signed OS packages (.deb for Ubuntu, .rpm for RHEL) by adding a [package] section to its vergil.toml. The section is optional. A repo without it builds no packages, does not call ci-package, and sees no change in CI or CD.

With [package] present:

  • vrg-validate checks the section and the optional overlay file (see Validation).
  • PR CI builds every package and install-tests it in a clean container of each target OS. The result is the package / evidence gate.
  • A release builds the same packages, signs them, attaches them to the GitHub release, and notifies the org's package repository, which indexes them.

The design is epic vergil-project/.github#356 (spec epics/356-binary-package-publishing/spec.md).

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
[package]
builder = "python"            # python | staged
vendor  = "vergil"            # install root /opt/<vendor>/<name>/
summary = "Shared development tooling for Vergil-managed repositories"
smoke   = "vrg-whoami --mode" # the install test runs this after install

# Target selection. Default: every registered target. Set at most one of:
# exclude = ["rhel/*/arm64"]  # drop targets (glob)
# targets = ["ubuntu/*/*"]    # explicit subset replacing the default

# native  = ["ubuntu/26.04/*"]  # own build cell, inside that OS
# name    = "..."               # required for staged; python defaults to pyproject [project].name
# version = "3.14.4+20261001"   # explicit package version; default: the repo version
# upstream-version = "3.15.1+20261021"  # upstream inputs; package version is <this>.<repo version>
# noarch  = true                # architecture-independent: built once, deb `all` / rpm `noarch`

[package.python]               # optional for builder = "python"
# runtime = "3.14.8"          # exact-patch pin; default: derived from the resolved version
# commands = ["vrg-git"]      # subset of [project.scripts] to shim; default: all

# For builder = "staged" instead of [package.python]:
# [package.staged]
# build-command = "packaging/build.sh"  # populates $VRG_STAGING_ROOT for $VRG_TARGET_ARCH

docs.title: Several packages: [[package]]
docs.text:
A repo that publishes more than one package declares each one as an entry in an array of tables, [[package]]. Each entry takes the same keys and subtables as a single [package]. A subtable such as [package.python] or [package.staged] belongs to the [[package]] entry directly above it.

[[package]]
name    = "example-server"
builder = "staged"
vendor  = "vergil"
summary = "Example server"
smoke   = "example-server --version"

[package.staged]
build-command = "packaging/build-server.sh"

[[package]]
name    = "example-client"
builder = "staged"
vendor  = "vergil"
summary = "Example client"
smoke   = "example-client --version"

[package.staged]
build-command = "packaging/build-client.sh"

A single [package] table is one entry and behaves exactly as before. A single [[package]] entry behaves the same as a [package] table. With more than one entry, vrg-validate (and every tool that reads vergil.toml) refuses the config unless:

  • every entry sets an explicit name, and no two entries share one. The pyproject.toml name fallback for builder = "python" applies only to a single package.
  • every entry has the same vendor. The release wait and the tracking issue resolve one <org>/packages repository from it.
  • the repo has no packaging/nfpm.overlay.yaml. That overlay has one fixed path, so it would apply to every package. It is allowed only with a single package.

The other repo-level checks run once per entry. For example, a python entry still requires uv.lock (see Validation).

Every stage handles each entry as its own package. The matrix qualifies every cell id with the package name (see Matrix resolution), vrg-package build --cell and install-test --cell pick the entry from the cell, so each package builds with its own builder and is install-tested with its own smoke, and check-runtime checks each python package against its own runtime (see One runtime per package).

At most one python entry may pin [package.python].runtime. Version resolution and vrg-update-deps read the pin from the packages list, and refuse a config where more than one entry pins a runtime, with several [[package]] entries pin a runtime; pin it on one entry. Any python entry, pinned or not, makes version resolution require a published vergil-python runtime (see [package.python]).

The design is epic vergil-project/.github#472 (spec epics/472-multi-series-runtime/spec.md, §5.1).

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Default Semantics builder string (required) python (a Python venv product) or staged (any pre-built tree) vendor string (required) Vendor directory: the product installs under /opt/<vendor>/<name>/ summary string (required) One-line package description smoke string (required) Shell command the install test runs after installing the package name string see semantics Package name. Required for staged; python defaults to pyproject.toml [project].name version string repo version Explicit package version ([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+~]*), used unchanged as the full package version, for when it is not the repo's semver. A release refuses a version an earlier release already published; see the re-publish check. Not with upstream-version upstream-version string (unset) The upstream inputs a package is built from ([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+~]*), for example 3.15.1+20261021. The package version is <upstream-version>.<repo version> (3.15.1+20261021.1.0.5 at repo 1.0.5), so every repo release publishes a new version and the inputs show first in apt policy. That version sorts above the same inputs without the suffix and above an earlier repo release, under both dpkg and rpm.
