Design: epic vergil-project/.github#167. The pinning doctrine is inherited from epic vergil-project/.github#155.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command What it does vrg-host / vrg-host status Read-only report of every host dependency (the default) vrg-host status --fix Run the remediation of each unsatisfied auxiliary check first, then report vrg-host upgrade <dep>… Upgrade the named dependencies vrg-host upgrade --all [--force] Upgrade every auto dependency, holding pinned ones unless --force vrg-host pin <dep> --constraint … --inducing-release … --reason … Hold a dependency back vrg-host unpin <dep> Free a pin (kept as history)

docs.title: status
docs.text:
For each dependency in the host-dependency manifest, status prints its install method, installed version, latest version, version state and severity, followed by any pin and auxiliary-check detail lines, and an overall: line. It changes nothing on the host (unless --fix is given).

Each dependency is classified on two axes, its version state and its auxiliary checks, and gets the worse of the two severities:

State Meaning Severity current Installed is at or newer than latest OK latest-unmanaged The manifest declares no latest feed; the installed version is shown as info OK pinned An active pin holds it, and the installed version satisfies the constraint (tracked debt) OK pinned An active pin holds it, but the installed version has drifted off the constraint, or the pin is due for re-evaluation WARN behind Installed is older than latest, unpinned (shown as "drift") WARN latest-unknown A latest-version probe that should work did not answer WARN missing Not installed (or not installed by the manifest's method) ERROR probe-error A probe answered but its output could not be read, two versions could not be ordered, or the entry could not be probed ERROR any state + an unsatisfied auxiliary check The tool is present but a health check fails ERROR

docs.title: Update levels (macOS)
docs.text:
Software Update can offer more than one macOS update at once, for example an update within the current major and the next major. For macos, status reports every level that is behind instead of only the newest:

[WARN ] macos            custom              26.5.2 -> 27.0.1       behind (drift): minor 26.7.1, major 27.0.1
  • Each offered version is classified against the installed one by the first component that differs: the first is a major update, the second a minor, and any later one a patch (26.5.2 with only 26.5.3 offered reads behind (drift): patch 26.5.3).
  • An offer that is not newer than the installed version is ignored. When several offers fall in the same level, the highest is shown.
  • The latest column shows the leading edge: the highest offer, or the installed version when nothing newer is offered (current).
  • Any level behind is WARN (drift); severity and exit codes are as for every other dependency. Only what Apple actually lists is reported. If a patch release has been superseded, Software Update stops listing it, and status does not invent it.
  • A macOS offer the probe cannot read (a title with no Version, or a version that is not dotted numeric, such as 26.7.1 (a)) is a probe-error, never dropped.

The Xcode Command Line Tools (xcode-clt) also come from Software Update, so they report update levels the same way, from the "Command Line Tools" items that softwareupdate --list lists:

[WARN ] xcode-clt        custom              26.6.0 -> 26.7         behind (drift): minor 26.7

Only macos and xcode-clt report update levels. Every other dependency compares against a single latest version.

A broken probe for one dependency becomes a probe-error row for that dependency only; the rest of the report still runs. Nothing is ever guessed at: an unreadable version is an error, never a false current or missing.

Exit code — the worst severity across all dependencies:

Exit Meaning 0 Everything OK (including tracked-debt pins and info-only rows) 1 At least one warning (drift, latest unknown, a pin needing attention) 2 At least one error (missing, probe error, unsatisfied check), a failed --fix remediation, or an unreadable manifest or pins file

--fix runs, before the report, the remediation of each unsatisfied auxiliary check on every installed dependency (a missing dependency is skipped and reported as missing). Each remediation is verified by re-running its check. A remediation that fails, or leaves its check unsatisfied, is printed to stderr and forces exit 2. Remediations run unprivileged like every other command.

docs.title: upgrade
docs.text:
vrg-host upgrade gh lima       # named dependencies
vrg-host upgrade --all         # every auto dependency
vrg-host upgrade --all --force # also upgrade past active pins

Name one or more dependencies or pass --all, not both.

  • Only upgrade = "auto" dependencies are upgraded, through their install method (brew upgrade, uv tool upgrade, or the manifest's own upgrade command). A manual dependency (docker-desktop, macos, xcode-clt) is refused when named, and listed as skipped under --all; upgrade it by hand.
  • A Homebrew cask that updates itself (its brew info JSON says auto_updates: true) is never upgraded through brew. Without --greedy, brew upgrade skips such a cask without saying so, so vrg-host reports the upgrade as failed instead.
  • An actively pinned dependency is held: the package managers cannot upgrade to a constraint, so the pin is a real hold. Run vrg-host unpin <dep> first, or pass --force to upgrade past it. An active pin whose constraint is unsupported is an error even under --force.
  • An upgrade that fails, or that would need elevated privileges, is reported for that dependency and never retried elevated. Upgrade it manually.

Before upgrading anything, upgrade probes each auto dependency's installed and latest versions and classifies them exactly as status does. It then prints one line per dependency saying what it actually did:

skipped  uv: current (0.13.1)
upgraded git: 2.54.0 -> 2.56.0_1
unchanged bash: still 5.3.9, latest 5.3.20 (the upgrade command succeeded but did not change the installed version)
ran      vergil-tooling: 2.1.244 -> 2.1.244 (unchanged; no latest feed)
held     gh: pinned to 2.40.x (2.41.0 breaks vrg-gh auth) at 2.40.1, holding back from 2.42.0; run 'vrg-host unpin gh' or pass --force to upgrade past the pin
ERROR    lima: missing (not installed by brew-formula); vrg-host upgrades, it does not install
skipped (upgrade = manual, upgrade by hand): docker-desktop, macos
Outcome When Severity skipped … current (<v>) Already current; the upgrade command is not run OK upgraded … <before> -> <after> Was behind; upgraded and reached the latest OK upgraded … (still behind latest <v>) Was behind; the version moved but is still older than the latest (or cannot be ordered against it) WARN unchanged … Was behind; the upgrade command succeeded but the installed version did not change WARN ran … <before> -> <after> (no latest feed) latest = "unmanaged": nothing to compare with, so the upgrade runs and the change is reported OK ran … (latest unknown: …) The latest probe did not answer (as status's latest-unknown) WARN held … Actively pinned and no --force; shows the installed version and the latest it holds back from WARN (not counted under --all) ERROR … missing / ERROR … probe-error Not installed, or a probe failed, as status reports it; the upgrade is not attempted ERROR ERROR … upgrade ran but … The installed version could not be re-probed after the upgrade ERROR

The after version is always re-probed after the upgrade runs, never assumed to be the latest. --force only upgrades past a pin. It never forces the upgrade of a dependency that is already current.

Exit code: 0 when everything requested was upgraded or already current (or, under --all, deliberately skipped or held); 1 when an explicitly named dependency was refused (manual or pinned), or an upgrade left a dependency behind (or ran with its latest unknown); 2 on any failure: an unknown dependency name, a missing dependency, a probe error, a failed or privilege-refused upgrade, an unsupported pin constraint, or an unreadable manifest or pins file.

docs.title: pin and unpin
docs.text:
vrg-host pin gh \
  --constraint 2.40.x \
  --inducing-release 2.41.0 \
  --reason "2.41.0 breaks vrg-gh auth" \
  --tracking-issue https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-tooling/issues/NNNN \
  --deterministic

vrg-host unpin gh
Flag Required Meaning <dep> yes A dependency declared in the manifest; anything else is refused --constraint yes The version range to hold to (see Constraint grammar) --inducing-release yes The release that broke us — the pin's anchor --reason yes Why the pin exists. A blank reason is refused (the justification gate) --tracking-issue no URL of the issue tracking the breakage --deterministic no The breakage reproduces deterministically (selects the re-evaluation path)

pin records an active pin stamped with today's date, replacing any earlier pin for the same dependency. unpin sets the pin's state to freed and keeps it in the pins file as history, so the file stays the audit trail of what was held back and why. Unpinning a dependency with no pin, or one already freed, is refused. Both commands exit 0 on success and 1 when refused.

docs.title: The host-dependency manifest
docs.text:
The list of host dependencies is a manifest packaged with vergil-tooling: src/vergil_tooling/data/host_dependencies.toml. It is tooling-owned and is never overridable by a repository, vergil.toml, or the current directory. This is a security invariant: the manifest carries shell commands for probes, upgrades and checks, and letting a repo supply them would be an arbitrary-code execution surface on the host. Changing the list means a vergil-tooling PR.

Each entry declares the dependency's method (brew-formula, brew-cask, uv-tool or custom), whether vrg-host may upgrade it (upgrade = "auto" or "manual"), whether it has a latest-version feed (latest = "probe" or "unmanaged"), and any auxiliary checks. A custom entry supplies its own installed, latest and upgrade commands. Its latest command is either latest_version, which prints one version, or latest_versions, which prints every offered version, one bare version per line, for update-level reporting. An entry may declare only one of the two, and latest_versions requires latest = "probe"; the manifest is refused at load otherwise. An entry with any other method can override only how its installed version is read. This is for a self-updating app, whose package-manager record goes stale.

A tool earns an entry only if Vergil development needs it on the macOS host itself. Current entries:

Dependency Method Upgrade Latest Why it is on the host uv brew-formula auto probe Installs and upgrades the vrg-* host tools gh brew-formula auto probe GitHub CLI under vrg-gh and the PR/issue workflows git brew-formula auto probe vrg-git, vrg-commit, the PR workflow, vrg-release and worktrees run it on the host bash brew-formula auto probe The host-side vrg-* tools and the hook-guard shim run it gcloud custom (gcloud components update) auto probe IAP tunnel for vrg-vm cloud sessions lima brew-formula auto probe Runs the local agent VMs vrg-vm creates docker-desktop brew-cask (installed version from the app) manual probe The container engine and docker CLI that vrg-container-run execs opentofu brew-formula auto probe Provisions cloud agent VMs for vrg-vm (preflight requires >= 1.8.0) git-cliff brew-formula auto probe Changelog generator vrg-release requires vergil-tooling uv-tool auto unmanaged The vrg-* host tools themselves claude-code brew-cask auto probe The host-side agent for out-of-sandbox work, such as reattaching an agent session with human access macos custom manual probe The host OS; a pending update is surfaced, never applied xcode-clt custom manual probe Xcode Command Line Tools: Homebrew needs them, even when full Xcode is installed; a pending update is surfaced, never applied

Notes on the entries:

  • uv is a Homebrew formula. On the macOS host uv is installed with Homebrew (brew install uv), and Homebrew builds have no uv self update, so vrg-host reads and upgrades it through brew. Its latest is Homebrew's stable version, which can trail Astral's newest release by a few days.
  • gcloud updates itself. It is installed from the Homebrew gcloud-cli cask, but the SDK's component manager owns its updates: vrg-host reads its core component version and upgrades it with gcloud components update. The SDK lives in a user-owned directory, so this needs no sudo. Homebrew's recorded cask version goes stale as the SDK updates itself. Never upgrade it with brew upgrade --greedy.
  • docker-desktop and macos are report-only. vrg-host tracks the Docker Desktop app, not the docker CLI (their version numbers differ). The installed version comes from the app's Info.plist, because Desktop updates itself and Homebrew's record goes stale. The latest comes from the docker-desktop cask (its 4.94.0,241994 reads as 4.94.0). So status shows when Desktop is behind, but upgrade leaves it to Desktop's own updater, which may install privileged helpers. Moving to a headless engine (Colima, podman, docker-engine over Lima) would make Docker an auto entry; that is follow-on work (vergil-project/.github#169). A pending macOS update is reported so it is applied deliberately, never by vrg-host. The macos probe reads softwareupdate --list and reports every pending update level.
  • git and bash are Homebrew's. On a Homebrew-first Mac, git resolves to /opt/homebrew/bin/git ahead of Apple's /usr/bin/git shim (which runs the CLT's or Xcode.app's git, whichever xcode-select -p selects), and bash to Homebrew's bash 5 ahead of Apple's /bin/bash 3.2. The copies that actually run are therefore not updated with macOS, so vrg-host tracks and upgrades them through brew.
  • xcode-clt is report-only. Homebrew cannot work without the Xcode Command Line Tools, so a missing CLT is an ERROR. Apple ships CLT updates through Software Update, separately from macOS. The installed version comes from pkgutil --pkg-info=com.apple.pkg.CLTools_Executables, which prints a version with a trailing build stamp (26.6.0.0.1781586589). vrg-host keeps only the first three components (26.6.0), the precision Software Update uses, so its Version: 26.6 reads as current and 26.7 as a minor update. The latest comes from the "Command Line Tools" items in softwareupdate --list. When Software Update lists none, the CLT is current. An item the probe cannot read is a probe-error, never dropped. A listed item that is not newer than the installed version is ignored, like any offer that is not an update. Install CLT updates with Software Update; vrg-host never applies them.
  • claude-code is upgraded through Homebrew. It is installed from the claude-code cask, which does not declare auto_updates (Homebrew API, checked 2026-10-16), so vrg-host upgrade claude-code runs brew upgrade --cask claude-code. If the cask ever becomes self-updating, the upgrade is refused (see upgrade) and the entry must become manual. It is on the host as the agent for out-of-sandbox work, such as reattaching an agent session on the Mac with human access. The original design excluded it as a personal tool; that was reversed in #3300.
  • vergil-tooling has no latest feed. It is installed from git, so uv's outdated feed cannot see new releases; status reports it as latest-unmanaged rather than a false current. vrg-host upgrade vergil-tooling runs uv tool upgrade vergil-tooling, which moves within the release line you installed.
  • Install method matters. Each entry assumes the install path verified on a real macOS host. A tool installed some other way (for example, uv from Astral's standalone installer) reads as missing for the brew and uv-tool methods; it is never reported as a false current.

Deliberately not in the manifest:

  • Linters (shellcheck, hadolint, yamllint, actionlint, markdownlint) — they run only inside the dev container via vrg-validate. Do not install them on the host.
  • ssh and other OS-provided tools — updated with macOS (the macos entry). jq ships with macOS. (git and bash are tracked, because the copies that run are Homebrew's.)
  • Full Xcode — nothing on the host needs more than the Command Line Tools.
  • az (Azure CLI) — only vrg-vm --provider azure needs it, and GCP is the provider in use. It gets an entry if Azure becomes a working provider.
  • nfpm, npm, language toolchains — container and CI only.
  • Homebrew itself, editors and other personal tools.
  • Everything else installed with Homebrew — only the curated entries above are tracked or upgraded, never a blanket brew upgrade.

docs.title: Auxiliary checks
docs.text:
A dependency can carry health checks beyond its version, each with an optional remediation that status --fix runs. An unsatisfied check is an ERROR.

Dependency Check What it verifies Remediation gcloud numpy-in-interpreter The Python interpreter gcloud runs on can import NumPy. Without it every IAP tunnel session prints an "install NumPy" warning and the tunnel is slower. pip install numpy into that interpreter, unprivileged

If the interpreter is externally managed (PEP 668), pip refuses the install. vrg-host reports that as a failed remediation rather than working around it; install NumPy into that interpreter yourself.

docs.title: Pinning host dependencies
docs.text:
The default for every host dependency is unpinned: float on the leading edge. vrg-host adopts the org-wide pinning doctrine of epic #155, which treats a pin as technical debt to be paid down, not a setting:

  1. Default is unpinned.
  2. A pin is a reaction, never a default — a reaction to a release breaking us.
  3. Every pin carries a written justification — vrg-host pin refuses a pin without --reason.
  4. Pin the least-specific version that solves the problem — 1.x, not the exact patch.
  5. When in doubt, set it free — unpin, see what breaks, and pin only the culprit.
  6. A pin is anchored to its inducing release and is re-evaluated when the leading edge moves past it — never permanent.

docs.title: Where pins live
docs.text:
Pins are your configuration, not package data. They live in ~/.config/vergil/host-pins.toml, next to identities.toml, and are overlaid onto the packaged manifest when status and upgrade run. (Pins are never written into the packaged manifest: that would modify the installed package and be lost on every reinstall.)

vrg-host pin and unpin manage the file; it looks like this:

[pin.gh]
constraint = "2.40.x"
inducing_release = "2.41.0"
deterministic = true
reason = "2.41.0 breaks vrg-gh auth"
state = "active"
tracking_issue = "https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-tooling/issues/NNNN"
pinned_date = "2026-10-15"

The fields are #155's pin schema plus one host extension, pinned_date, so status can show how long a pin has stood. A pin's state is active (holds the dependency), under-evaluation (shown in status but not holding), or freed (history). vrg-host pin only creates active pins; moving a pin to under-evaluation is a hand edit of this file.

The file is validated strictly. A missing file means "no pins". It is an error (exit 2 from status and upgrade) if the file is not valid TOML, has keys other than [pin.<dep>] tables, pins a dependency the manifest does not declare, or has a pin without a reason. The pins file can only hold back declared dependencies; it cannot add dependencies or change their methods, probes or checks.

docs.title: Constraint grammar
docs.text:
A constraint is a dotted version prefix, optionally ending in x wildcards:

Constraint Matches 1.x any 1.* release 2.40.x any 2.40.* release 2.40.0 exactly 2.40.0 (a Homebrew rebuild such as 2.40.0_1 also matches)

Any other syntax — >=, <=, ~=, an x that is not trailing, empty components — is refused when you run vrg-host pin, never guessed at.

docs.title: How a pin is surfaced
docs.text: status renders each active pin as tracked debt under its dependency's row: the constraint, the latest version it is holding back from (the size of the debt), the inducing release, the reason, the tracking issue, and the pin's age. For macos, the row still lists every pending update level, so an update the pin allows (such as 26.7.1 under a 26.x pin) stays visible.

docs.title: Re-evaluation
docs.text:
A pin is valid only while its inducing release is the leading edge. When the latest available version moves past inducing_release, status marks the pin RE-EVALUATION DUE and the row becomes WARN. For macos, the latest is the leading edge: the highest version Software Update offers. If the latest version is unknown, or the two versions cannot be compared, it shows RE-EVALUATION UNKNOWN (also WARN). For a dependency with no latest feed, it reminds you to check the leading edge by hand.

When a pin is due, follow the #155 process:

  • Deterministic breakage (deterministic = true) — re-test against the new leading edge. If it works, vrg-host unpin the dependency; if it still breaks, re-pin with the new release as --inducing-release.
  • Non-deterministic breakage — move the pin to under-evaluation under a tracking issue and observe.

docs.title: No privilege escalation
docs.text: vrg-host runs as the ordinary user. It refuses to run any command that starts with sudo, doas, su or pkexec, and gives every child process a closed stdin, so a command that unexpectedly asks for a password fails instead of prompting. An upgrade or remediation that needs elevated privileges is reported as needing manual action and is never retried elevated.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The version parsers are tested against output captured on a real Mac. A few cases could not be captured there and are still hand-written: softwareupdate with nothing pending, only non-OS updates pending, or only a patch update pending, and uv tool list --outdated listing an outdated tool. The Command Line Tools update offer (softwareupdate --list listing a CLT item newer than the installed one) and the full pkgutil --pkg-info output are hand-written as well: only the CLT version: line was recorded. See tests/vergil_tooling/fixtures/host/README.md. If one of those cases shows a probe-error row, it may be a parser mismatch rather than a broken tool.
  • vrg-host reports and acts only when you run it. Scheduled or automatic runs are follow-on work (vergil-project/.github#169).

docs.title: vrg-pr-fix-body
docs.text:
Installed as: vrg-pr-fix-body (Python console script)

Source: src/vergil_tooling/bin/vrg_pr_fix_body.py

Repair a PR's body through the same validated builder that vrg-submit-pr uses to create it. The body is regenerated from corrected fields — summary, issue reference, linkage, notes — so a body can only ever be replaced by a standards-compliant body. Free-form PR edits (gh pr edit) remain denied for agent identities; this tool is the narrow repair path that restores what the pr-watch reconcile loop needs without reopening structural PR mutation.

Why this exists

A standards failure on the PR body (for example a forbidden auto-close linkage keyword) is a failing CI check that no code patch can fix. The pr-watch USER agent is chartered to reconcile failing checks, so it needs a safe way to fix its own PR's body. See issue #1459.

docs.title: Identity rules
docs.text: Identity Allowed Scope audit No The audit identity never mutates PRs user Yes Only its own PR: the PR's head branch must match the session's current branch human Yes Any PR (the human is the superset)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vrg-pr-fix-body PR --issue NUMBER --summary TEXT [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Required Description pr Yes PR number or URL --issue Yes Issue number or cross-repo ref --summary Yes One-line PR summary --linkage No Linkage keyword (default: Ref) --notes No Additional notes for the PR --dry-run No Print the regenerated body without editing --no-retrigger No Skip the empty-commit push that re-runs CI

docs.title: Linkage Keywords
docs.text: Ref

docs.title: CI re-trigger
docs.text: A body edit alone does not re-run the standards gate: pull_request workflows trigger on opened/synchronize/reopened (not edited), and a manual re-run replays the stale event payload. After editing the body, the tool therefore pushes an empty commit so CI re-runs against the corrected body. Pass --no-retrigger to skip this and push your own commit instead.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Preview the regenerated body
vrg-pr-fix-body 1457 --issue 1450 --summary "Port vrg-vm to progress" --dry-run

# Fix the body and re-trigger CI
vrg-pr-fix-body https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1457 \
  --issue 1450 \
  --summary "Port vrg-vm lifecycle commands to the progress framework" \
  --notes "Body-only fix: replaced auto-close linkage with Ref"

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Denies the audit identity.
  2. Validates the issue reference and regenerates the body via the shared builder (vergil_tooling.lib.pr_body); the linkage keyword is constrained to the allowed set.
  3. --dry-run: prints the body and stops.
  4. Agent identities: verifies the PR's head branch matches the session's current branch.
  5. Verifies the PR is open.
  6. Replaces the body via gh pr edit --body-file.
  7. Pushes an empty commit to re-trigger CI (unless --no-retrigger).

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Body replaced (and CI re-triggered unless --no-retrigger) 1 Identity/scope/state rejection or validation failure

docs.title: vrg-release
docs.text:
Installed as: vrg-release (Python console script)

Source: src/vergil_tooling/bin/vrg_release.py (stages in src/vergil_tooling/lib/release/orchestrator.py)

Runs the whole release workflow from develop to main: preflight, tracking issue, changelog, release PR, merge, CD confirmation, back-merge and version bump, rolling-tag promotion, cleanup, consumer refresh, and the post-release dependency update. The stages and what they leave behind are described in the Releasing guide.

Releasing is a human maintainer action. vrg-release refuses to run under an agent identity.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vrg-release [minor|major] [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Required Description minor / major No Bump to the next minor or major version before releasing. Default: release the current develop version --no-promote No Skip moving the rolling vX.Y tag --without-deps No Skip the update-deps stage --allow-pending-deps No Release even though an open dependency-update PR blocks it. For urgent fixes only; the bypassed PRs are listed on the tracking issue --install No After a clean release, run the [publish].consumer-refresh commands instead of only printing them. Fails if none are configured --resume [X.Y.Z] No Resume an interrupted release from its open tracking issue. Name the version when more than one release is in flight. Cannot be combined with minor/major --skip-audit No Skip the audit stage --output-window N No Rolling output window for the terminal renderer (0 streams everything) --output-format No Force the renderer: rich, gha or plain

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Run from the root checkout, on develop, with a clean working tree that matches origin/develop.
  • git-cliff on PATH and an authenticated gh.

docs.title: The dependency-update gate
docs.text: On a fresh start (not on --resume), preflight refuses while an open PR carries the dependency-update label. First it closes, with a comment, any such PR whose linked fix task was closed as completed (the update landed through the fix PR), and deletes its head branch. A failed branch delete is reported, not fatal. --allow-pending-deps lets the release past whatever still blocks. Lookup failures refuse the release. See The dependency-update gate.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Every stage succeeded 1 A stage failed, including a deferred failure such as a missed publish job or a failed dependency update; or the command was refused 130 Interrupted (Ctrl-C)

docs.title: vrg-security-record
docs.text:
Installed as: vrg-security-record (Python console script)

Source: src/vergil_tooling/bin/vrg_security_record.py (library: src/vergil_tooling/lib/security_records.py)

Records a security finding as a pair: a private draft repository security advisory in <org>/.github that holds the details, and a neutral security-labelled intake issue that carries only a pointer to it. For the policy, neutral wording and the severity mapping, see Security Records.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vrg-security-record create --repo OWNER/NAME --title TEXT --body-file FILE
                           --details-file FILE --severity {critical,high,medium,low}
                           [--summary TEXT] [--issue OWNER/REPO#N] [--resume GHSA-ID]
vrg-security-record list [--repo OWNER/NAME] [--state {draft,closed,all}] [--details]
vrg-security-record show (GHSA-ID | OWNER/REPO#N)
vrg-security-record retarget GHSA-ID --to OWNER/REPO#N [--to OWNER/REPO#N ...]

docs.title: Output rule
docs.text:
An advisory's summary and description reach stdout only through show and list --details, both meant for an interactive terminal. Every other line, and every error message, names only GHSA IDs, issue refs, labels and states. A failed GitHub call is reported with its exit status, command and stderr; its response body is dropped, because for an advisory call it may hold the advisory text.

list --details is refused when VRG_EPIC_SWEEP is set, so advisory text can never reach the scheduled sweep's public Actions logs.

docs.title: Where things are created
docs.text:
• --repo always names the affected repo, never where anything is created.
  • The advisory is always created in <org>/.github, where <org> is the owner of --repo (or of the --to refs for retarget). The command checks that <org>/.github is public and otherwise refuses with:
vrg-security-record: <org>/.github is not public; security records need a public org .github (private orgs are unsupported)
  • The issue is created in the affected repo's queue home (<org>/.github for a public repo, the repo itself for a private one) and linked under that home's intake epic, which is created if absent.

Every run scopes its GitHub App token to <org>. In human mode the human's own gh login is used.

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Creates the pair, or finishes one.

Flag Meaning --repo OWNER/NAME Required. The affected repo. Its bare name becomes the advisory's package name (ecosystem other). --title TEXT Required. The neutral issue title. --body-file FILE Required. The neutral issue body. The Security advisory: line is appended to it. --details-file FILE Required. The private details; sent only to the advisory, as its description. --severity LEVEL Required. critical, high, medium or low. --summary TEXT The advisory summary, at most 1024 characters. Default: the first line of the details file. An empty summary is refused. --issue OWNER/REPO#N Attach mode: use this existing issue instead of creating one. --resume GHSA-ID Finish the pair of this existing advisory instead of creating a new one.

A fresh create runs these steps in order:

  1. Duplicate guard. Look for a draft in <org>/.github with the same summary and the same affected repo. If one exists, refuse, naming its GHSA ID and the command that finishes its pair.
  2. Advisory. Create the draft. The request is sent exactly once, with no retry: drafts can't be deleted, so a retried create could leave a second record. It never publishes, never requests a CVE and never creates a private fork.
  3. Issue. Ensure the security label in the queue home, then create the issue there with the label and the body plus Security advisory: <org>/.github <GHSA-id>.
  4. Link. Add the issue as a sub-issue of the queue home's intake epic.
  5. Tracking line. Write Tracking issue: <owner>/<repo>#<N> into the advisory's description.

On success it prints Recorded <GHSA-id> in <org>/.github, tracked by <owner>/<repo>#<N>.

Failure. Every failure exits 1 and says what exists:

  • If creating the advisory fails, nothing else was created. If the draft was in fact created (a lost response), a re-run is refused by the duplicate guard, which names its GHSA ID.
  • If any later step fails, the message names the advisory, the step that failed, and the exact command that finishes the pair: the same arguments plus --resume <GHSA-id>, and --issue <ref> once the issue exists. --summary is left out of that command, since no advisory is created on resume. Run the printed command; never re-run the original.

Attach mode (--issue without --resume) attaches a new advisory to an existing issue instead of creating one. It adds the security label and the Security advisory: line to that issue, then writes the tracking line. The issue keeps its current parent. The past-issues audit uses this so that one problem never gets two issues.

Resume (--resume) skips the duplicate guard and the advisory, and completes whatever steps are missing:

  • with --issue, it marks that issue (idempotent), links it under the intake epic only if it has no parent yet, and writes the tracking line;
  • without --issue, it looks among the intake epic's sub-issues for one whose body has the advisory's Security advisory: line (it never uses search, whose index can lag). If none is found it creates the issue and links it. Then it writes the tracking line.

Every step is idempotent, so running a resume command twice is safe.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Lists the records in the org's .github, one line per advisory, sorted by GHSA ID:

GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx  draft  vergil-tooling  tracks: vergil-project/.github#123
GHSA-yyyy-yyyy-yyyy  triage  (no affected repo)  tracks: (no tracking issue)  [external report]

Each line has the GHSA ID, the advisory state, the affected repo (its package name) and the tracked issues. [external report] marks an advisory that came from private vulnerability reporting (the triage state or a submission).

Flag Meaning --repo OWNER/NAME Only advisories about this affected repo. Its owner selects the org. Without it, the org is taken from the current repo's origin remote. --state STATE draft, closed or all. Default: all, which includes every state (also triage, published and withdrawn). --details Also print each advisory's summary on an indented summary: line. Interactive use only; refused when VRG_EPIC_SWEEP is set.

With no match it prints No security records in <org>/.github match.

docs.title: show
docs.text:
Prints pairs with their details, to the terminal: for each, the list line, then summary: and description: with the advisory's text.

  • show GHSA-ID prints that one pair. It takes the org from the current repo's origin remote.
  • show OWNER/REPO#N reads every Security advisory: line in that issue's body and prints one pair per advisory, in body order, separated by a blank line. It uses the issue's owner as the org. An issue with no such line is refused with <owner>/<repo>#<N> has no Security advisory: line.

If any advisory to print does not exist in <org>/.github, show refuses and prints no pair at all, not even the ones that exist. The refusal names every missing advisory:

vrg-security-record: advisory GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx does not exist in vergil-project/.github
vrg-security-record: advisories GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, GHSA-yyyy-yyyy-yyyy do not exist in vergil-project/.github

docs.title: retarget
docs.text:
Moves an advisory's tracking to new issues. It is the one way a link moves; vrg-intake-route and the epic-create planning handoff both use it.

vrg-security-record retarget GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx \
  --to vergil-project/vergil-tooling#101 --to vergil-project/vergil-tooling#102

Every --to must be a full owner/repo#N ref, and all of them must be in one org. The steps run in order, and each starts only once the one before it succeeded:

  1. Mark each target: ensure the security label in its repo, add it to the issue, and append the Security advisory: line (skipped when already present).
  2. Rewrite the advisory's description: every Tracking issue: line is replaced by one line per target. The rest of the description is kept.
  3. Unmark every issue that names this advisory but is no longer a target. These are the issues in the old tracking lines, plus every security-labelled issue in the org whose Security advisory: line names this GHSA ID (found by REST listing, never by search). Each one gets the comment Security record moved to <refs> (posted once, even on a re-run). Then this advisory's line is removed, together with the security label when no other advisory line remains, in one edit. An issue that also names other advisories keeps their lines and the label. An issue that names only other advisories is never touched.

An issue naming several advisories needs one retarget per advisory. Run them one after another, never in parallel: each rewrites the issue's body, so two at once can write back a line the other removed. They can run in either order; the label goes only with the last line.

A failure at any step exits 1 with a message naming the advisory and the step. Because a later step never runs before an earlier one succeeds, an advisory never ends up tracking an issue that lacks the label and line. After a failure at any step, re-run the same command: it finishes the job. An issue that still carries this advisory's line and label is found again by the listing, so an interrupted unmark is completed. The one case a re-run cannot reach is an issue whose security label was removed by hand while its advisory line stayed; the sweep reports it as a broken pair. On success it prints Retargeted <GHSA-id> to <refs>.

The library's retarget also takes a renamed= list, which the CLI does not expose. vrg-intake-route uses it for a transfer: the old number of a transferred issue is replaced in the tracking lines but never unmarked, because the old number now leads to the moved issue itself.

docs.title: Related commands
docs.text:
These commands read or move records as part of their own work:

  • vrg-epic-audit --close (the scheduled sweep) syncs each paired advisory's state to its issues and reports broken pairs. It only moves an advisory between draft and closed: it never changes a published, withdrawn or triage advisory, or an unpaired external report, which it lists as unpaired external report (left untouched). Its summary line is Security records: <n> advisory state(s) synced, <m> broken pair(s). It exits 1 when any pair is broken (after syncing the rest), or when the pass fails, including when the org's .github is private. An org with no security issues and no .github repo prints Security records: none. The read-only vrg-epic-audit prints the same pass as a (preview) with would sync, makes no change, and does not fail on a broken pair.
  • vrg-intake-route retargets a security item's advisories on a transfer, a recreate or a split. A transfer or recreate retargets every advisory the item names, in body order. A recreate retargets before the original closes and stops with the original open on failure; a transfer retargets after the move and, on failure, names every advisory still not retargeted with the retarget command for each. A split retargets the item's one advisory before the original closes and stops with the original open on failure; a split of an item naming several advisories is refused before any change, naming their GHSA IDs, since which advisory goes to which task can't be inferred. An item with the security label but no advisory line, or the reverse, gets a warning and no retarget.
  • vrg-queue planning keeps a planning issue at in-progress while any advisory it names still tracks it, with a note that counts them and names them by GHSA ID only (advisory still tracks for one, advisories still track for more):
held: <k> advisories still track this planning issue (<GHSA-id>[, …]) — retarget each to the task or tasks that fix it with vrg-security-record retarget

It reads the advisories only when some planning item names one.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Refused (a private .github, a duplicate, bad refs, an unreadable file, --details under the sweep), a partial pair, a failed retarget, a GitHub API failure, or an authentication failure 2 Invalid arguments

docs.title: vrg-submit-pr
docs.text:
Installed as: vrg-submit-pr (Python console script)

Source: src/vergil_tooling/bin/vrg_submit_pr.py

Wrapper that creates standards-compliant pull requests with proper issue linkage. Has three modes:

  • Template mode (no arguments) — the normal path. Reads .vergil/pr-workflow.json (the oracle state file the agent records via vrg-pr-workflow), shows a preview, asks for confirmation, pushes the branch, creates the PR, and emits the /vergil:pr-watch handoff line.
  • Relay branch mode (positional <branch> [<branch> …]) — the Mac side of the cloud→Mac relay handoff (issue #2368). Opens PRs for branches that are already on origin, worktree-free: each branch's ready-state is resolved from a local worktree's pr-workflow.json when one exists, else fetched from the relay ref refs/vergil/pr-workflow/<branch> that report-ready always pushes. Origin's tip is verified against the recorded head_sha and the PR is opened without pushing (--head names the source branch). No worktree, no git.current_branch(), and no push are involved — the branch and its metadata already rode GitHub.
  • CLI mode (--issue/--summary/--title) — direct invocation for human emergency use.

Human-run tool

PR submission is a human action. Agent identities are blocked; agents hand off via .vergil/pr-workflow.json instead.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: When running inside a dev container, GH_TOKEN must be set so gh can authenticate. The Getting Started prerequisites cover gh auth login and how GH_TOKEN flows through to the container.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Template mode (normal): from the repo root or inside the worktree
vrg-submit-pr

# Relay branch mode (cloud handoff): worktree-free, from the main worktree
vrg-submit-pr <branch> [<branch> …]

# CLI mode (emergency): from inside the worktree
vrg-submit-pr --issue NUMBER --summary TEXT --title TEXT [options]

docs.title: Running from the repo root
docs.text:
In template mode, vrg-submit-pr may be run from the repo root — it resolves the target worktree itself:

  • One submittable worktree (contains .vergil/pr-workflow.json): announced and entered automatically; the usual preview + [y/N] confirmation follows.
  • Several submittable worktrees: a numbered menu shows each worktree with its issue number and title; pick one.
  • None: an error lists each worktree and why it was skipped.

Run from inside a worktree, behavior is unchanged. The tool is interactive by design — it is a human touch point of the workflow and requires a terminal; root launches fail fast when stdin is not a TTY.

docs.title: Relay branch mode (cloud-to-Mac handoff)
docs.text:
Passing one or more branch names opens PRs worktree-free for work an off-platform (cloud x86) agent implemented and pushed. It is the Mac side of the GitHub relay: the cloud VM and the Mac never share a disk, so the agent's report-ready mirrors its ready-state onto the reserved ref refs/vergil/pr-workflow/<branch> in addition to the local .vergil/pr-workflow.json. Run from the main worktree:

vrg-submit-pr feature/123-x feature/124-y

For each branch, the tool:

  1. resolves the ready-state from a local worktree's pr-workflow.json when one exists, else fetches it from the relay ref;
  2. verifies the tip of origin/<branch> matches the recorded head_sha (a mismatch fails loudly — the metadata is for a different commit);
  3. opens the PR with --head <branch> and does not push — the branch is already on origin.

The relay ref is world-readable

On a public repo, anyone can read refs/vergil/pr-workflow/<branch>. Keep secrets out of the report-ready --title, --summary, and --notes — they are public the moment they are recorded.

The relay ref is cleaned up by vrg-finalize-pr, which deletes it alongside the branch on merge and sweeps any orphaned relay ref whose branch no longer exists.

docs.title: Cascade on the relay path (--finalize/--release/--install)
docs.text:
The relay path runs the full cascade too (issue #2398): the cascade is a local macOS action, so it does not matter whether the branch was implemented on the Mac or on a cloud VM. Once the PR is open, finalizing, releasing, and installing operate on the PR and the remote — the branch does not need to be checked out locally (vrg-finalize-pr already merges and cleans up a branch with no local worktree).

# Open PRs for both cloud-implemented branches, then merge, release, and
# install — all locally, in one command.
vrg-submit-pr --install feature/123-x feature/124-y

It uses the same batch semantics as the worktree batch (--all / --select): each PR is finalized in turn, then — only if every branch merged — a single end-of-batch post-checks step (validation + CD check) runs, followed by one vrg-release (never one per branch). A branch that already carries a submitted PR is fail-fast in the cascade (finalize it directly with vrg-finalize-pr <url>); without a cascade flag it is simply reported and skipped, as before.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Required (CLI mode) Description --issue Yes Issue number or cross-repo ref --summary Yes One-line PR summary --title Yes PR title --linkage No Linkage keyword (default: Ref) --notes No Additional notes for the PR --base No Override the auto-detected target branch --dry-run No Print PR body without executing --finalize No After creating the PR, chain straight into vrg-finalize-pr

docs.title: Linkage Keywords
docs.text: Ref

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Normal flow: resolve the worktree, preview, confirm
vrg-submit-pr

# Relay branch mode: open PRs for cloud-implemented branches, worktree-free
vrg-submit-pr feature/123-x feature/124-y

# Preview without submitting
vrg-submit-pr --dry-run

# Emergency CLI mode
vrg-submit-pr \
  --issue 42 \
  --summary "Add new lint check for X" \
  --title "feat(lint): add new check for X"

# Submit and merge-on-green in one step
vrg-submit-pr --finalize

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Template mode from the repo root: resolves the target worktree (see above) and moves into it — the invoking shell is unaffected.
  2. Reads .vergil/pr-workflow.json (template mode) or validates CLI arguments, including the issue reference format.
  3. Detects target branch from the current branch:
    • release/* branches target main
    • All other branches target develop
  4. Shows the PR preview and asks Submit this PR? [y/N] (template mode).
  5. Pushes the branch to origin with the human's host credentials.
  6. Creates the PR via gh pr create and deletes the template.
  7. Prints the PR URL — which can be passed straight to vrg-finalize-pr.

docs.title: Chaining into finalize (--finalize)
docs.text:
--finalize folds the manual two-command sequence (vrg-submit-pr, then vrg-finalize-pr <pr>) into one step: after the PR is created, the tool hands off to the vrg-finalize-pr wait-and-merge flow from the main worktree root. Use it when the decision to merge-on-green has already been made at submit time.

Semantics are identical to running vrg-finalize-pr <pr-url> by hand (same merge-strategy default, same post-merge cleanup), and the failure modes split cleanly:

  • A submit failure stops before finalize runs — no half-finalized state.
  • A finalize failure leaves the created PR unaffected and prints it clearly so you can re-run vrg-finalize-pr <pr-url> alone.

Like the rest of the tool, --finalize is human-only — the agent identity gate runs before either mode.

docs.title: Batch mode (--all / --select)
docs.text:
Selecting two or more ready worktrees submits them as a single serialized batch (issue #1673). Use --all for every ready worktree, or --select <tokens> for a comma-separated subset matched by issue number or worktree directory name (e.g. --select 1673,1681); an unmatched or ambiguous token is a hard error that names it. A single selection runs the unchanged single-PR path.

The batch is optimized so each expensive CI gate runs exactly once. For each worktree in turn it:

  1. rebases the branch onto the latest develop — the step that guarantees the gate runs against the final state, so a later merge is never BEHIND and never re-runs CI;
  2. submits the PR;
  3. with --finalize/--release/--install, finalizes it (vrg-finalize-pr <url> --skip-post-checks — merge and cleanup, deferring validation).

After every item merges, post-merge validation and the CD check run once, then — with --release/--install — a single vrg-release ships all the changes in one version bump.

The batch asks one confirmation up front (skipped with --yes), then runs unattended. It is fail-fast: the first failure (rebase conflict, red gate, merge conflict, provenance violation) stops the batch and prints a merged / failed / not started summary. Already-merged PRs stay merged; re-running picks up only the remaining ready worktrees.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 PR created (and, with --finalize, merged and cleaned up) 1 Validation failure, declined confirmation, or no submittable worktree other With --finalize: the PR was created but finalize failed — re-run vrg-finalize-pr alone

docs.title: vrg-update-deps
docs.text:
Installed as: vrg-update-deps (Python console script)

Source: src/vergil_tooling/bin/vrg_update_deps.py (pipeline in src/vergil_tooling/lib/update_deps/)

Updates a repo's dependencies to the newest versions their declared bounds allow, validates once, and drives the result through a PR to merge. Every vrg-release already runs the same pipeline as its update-deps stage (see Dependency updates), so run this command by hand only when you want an update outside a release, or to move the repo to a new vergil series with --vergil.

vrg-update-deps merges its own PR, so it is human-only: it refuses to run under an agent identity.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vrg-update-deps [--only NAME[,NAME] | --skip NAME[,NAME] | --vergil X.Y]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
Argument Required Description --only NAME[,NAME] No Run only these updaters --skip NAME[,NAME] No Run every applicable updater except these --vergil X.Y No Move the repo to vergil series X.Y. Runs only the vergil updater, in bump mode --output-window N No Rolling output window for the terminal renderer (0 streams everything) --output-format No Force the renderer: rich, gha or plain

--only, --skip and --vergil are mutually exclusive. The updater names are python, vergil, images and hook; an unknown name is an error. The updaters are described in the dependency-update reference.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Run from the root checkout, on develop, with a clean working tree that matches origin/develop.
  • An authenticated gh.
  • No dependency update for the current develop version may be in flight. See An existing update branch.

docs.title: An existing update branch
docs.text:
If the deps/update-<version> branch for the current develop version already exists locally or on origin, preflight looks up the branch's PRs and acts on the newest one:

Branch state What preflight does The PR merged The update for this version is already done. It prints the PR's URL and exits 0 without updating anything The PR was closed without merging The branch is stale. It deletes the branch on origin and locally, naming it, then runs the update as usual A PR is open Refuses: the update is still in flight. Land or close the PR first The branch has no PR Refuses: the update is still in flight

preflight also refuses, without deleting anything, when the branch's tip is not the head of its newest PR. That means the branch name was reused after the PR finished, so the branch holds commits that no PR covers. If a stale branch cannot be deleted, preflight refuses and names the branch to delete by hand.

After it merges its own PR, the merge stage deletes the deps/update-<version> branch on origin. GitHub's delete-on-merge setting usually deletes it first, and the stage then reports that it is already gone. If the delete fails, the stage prints a warning with the command to run by hand. The run still succeeds, because the update has merged.

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
Stage What it does preflight Checks the prerequisites and creates the deps/update-<version> managed worktree update Runs each applicable updater in order (python, vergil, images, then hook), committing each one's changes separately validate Runs vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate once, if anything changed prepare-pr Pushes the branch and opens a PR to develop labelled dependency-update, creating the label if the repo lacks it merge Waits for the PR's checks and merges it, if validation passed, then deletes its branch on origin fix-task After any failure, files the fix task; after a validation or merge failure, also links it from the PR body finalize Prints the held-back report and removes the worktree and local branch status Exits non-zero if a failure was recorded

When no updater changes anything, no branch is pushed and no PR is opened.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
• update: an updater or the hook failed. Nothing is pushed and no PR is opened, but a "Fix failed dependency update for <version>" task is filed under the repo's ad-hoc epic. It names the failing updater and carries the error and the command to reproduce it on develop. With no labelled PR, it does not gate the next vrg-release.
  • validation or merge: the PR stays open with its dependency-update label, a "Fix failed dependency update for <version>" task is filed under the repo's ad-hoc epic, and the PR body gets a Fix task: <url> line and a failure section. While that PR is open, the next vrg-release refuses to start; see The dependency-update gate.

A re-run at the same develop version that fails the same way (the same failure kind) does not file a second task. The new failure is added as a comment on the open task, and that task is the one linked from the PR body and the run summary. If the lookup for an open task fails, the run fails rather than risk filing a duplicate.

The fix flow is in When the dependency update fails.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Updated and merged, nothing to update, or the update for this develop version had already merged 1 A failure was recorded, a precondition failed, or the command was refused 130 Interrupted (Ctrl-C)

docs.title: Claude Code Hook Guard
docs.text:
Path: .claude/hooks/guard.sh

The hook guard is a Claude Code PreToolUse hook that blocks raw git and gh commands in agent sessions. It delegates to vrg-hook-guard (when vergil-tooling is installed) or falls back to a jq-based hard deny.

The five branch/context checks below live in vrg-commit itself and run before git commit is invoked:

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: vrg-commit runs five checks in order:

docs.title: 1. Detached HEAD
docs.text: Commits on a detached HEAD are blocked unconditionally.

docs.title: 2. Protected Branch
docs.text: Direct commits to develop, release, and main are forbidden.

docs.title: 3. Branch Prefix Validation
docs.text:
Allowed prefixes depend on [project].branching-model in vergil.toml:

Branching Model Allowed Prefixes docs-single-branch feature/*, bugfix/*, chore/* application-promotion feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, promotion library-release feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release

An unrecognized branching model is an error. Without a vergil.toml, vrg-commit warns and falls back to feature/*, bugfix/* and chore/*.

docs.title: 4. Issue Number Naming
docs.text:
Work branches (feature/*, bugfix/*, hotfix/*, chore/*) must include a repository issue number:

{type}/{issue}-{description}

Example: feature/42-add-caching

release/* and promotion/* branches are exempt from this check because they are created by automated workflows.

docs.title: 5. Main-worktree commits
docs.text: When the repository has a .worktrees/ directory (the worktree convention), commits on a work branch from the main worktree are forbidden. Make them from a worktree under .worktrees/<name>/.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 All checks passed 1 Validation failure

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The hook guard is wired via .claude/settings.json and requires no per-clone setup. vrg-commit reads the branching model from [project].branching-model in vergil.toml. No other configuration is required.

docs.title: Markdown Validation
docs.text: Markdown validation is handled by vrg-validate (common checks) as part of the standard validation pipeline. It runs markdownlint against published documentation using a canonical config bundled in vergil-tooling.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Validation targets published markdown only:

Source Pattern Documentation site docs/site/**/*.md Project README README.md

Other markdown files (changelogs, release notes, internal docs) are not validated by this check.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The canonical config is bundled at src/vergil_tooling/configs/markdownlint.yaml and resolved at runtime via importlib.resources. Consuming repos do not need a local .markdownlint.yaml -- the bundled config applies everywhere.

default: true
no-duplicate-heading:
  siblings_only: true
MD013:
  line_length: 100
  tables: false
  code_blocks: false
MD060: false

Key rules:

Rule Setting Rationale Line length (MD013) 100 chars Matches ruff line-length setting Tables Exempt from line length Wide reference tables are legitimate Code blocks Exempt from line length Pasted commands and snippets exceed it Duplicate headings Siblings only Same heading text is fine across sections Table column style (MD060) Disabled No reader benefit for strict pipe alignment

docs.title: How it runs
docs.text:
vrg-validate runs common checks, which:

  1. Discovers markdown files matching the scope above.
  2. Resolves the bundled markdownlint.yaml config.
  3. Invokes markdownlint --config <bundled-config> <files...>.

This runs inside the dev container where markdownlint is on PATH.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 All files pass Non-zero One or more validation failures

docs.title: vrg-repo-profile
docs.text:
Installed as: vrg-repo-profile (Python console script)

Validates the repository configuration in vergil.toml and the structure of README.md. vrg-validate runs it as part of its common checks.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vrg-repo-profile

Run from the repository root. The script reads vergil.toml and README.md relative to the current directory.

docs.title: vergil.toml checks
docs.text:
vergil.toml is parsed with the same loader every vrg-* tool uses, and any value that loader rejects fails the check. The core rules:

Key Rule [project].repository-type Required; one of application, documentation, infrastructure, library, tooling (see Repository type and versions) [project].versioning-scheme Required; one of application, library, none, semver [project].branching-model Required; one of application-promotion, docs-single-branch, library-release [project].release-model Required; one of artifact-publishing, environment-promotion, none, tagged-release [project].ghas Optional; must be a boolean [ci].versions Optional pin; when set, a non-empty list of strings [ci].primary-version Optional; a string [dependencies].vergil Required

The recognized [project].primary-language values are cpp, go, java, python, rust and typescript. A retired language (ruby) is rejected outright. Any other unrecognized value is a warning, not a failure: the language is treated as unset. Unrecognized sections and keys are also reported as warnings. The optional tables have their own references, such as [container], [test] and [package].

docs.title: Repository type and versions
docs.text:
A repo's CI versions come from the language version window that vergil-containers publishes as window.json, read at the repo's [dependencies].vergil ref (see Version resolution). [project].repository-type decides how many of them the repo builds:

Type Resolves as Builds library library Every version in the window application, infrastructure, tooling, documentation app One version: the newest in the window

A library is a repo whose code runs in other repos' environments, whether imported there or installed there as a tool, so it must work on every supported version.

[ci].versions is an optional pin that replaces the default:

  • every pinned version must be in the window;
  • an app pin must name exactly one version;
  • C++ and TypeScript versions carry a compiler or runtime family (clang-20, gcc-14, node-24), so those repos must pin.

Each violation is an error. [ci].primary-version, when set, must name a resolved version; without it the primary is the newest resolved version.

vrg-repo-profile checks only the shape of these keys. The window rules are enforced by the resolver (lib/versions/resolve.py), which vrg-validate, vrg-container-run and the CI setup step (vrg-ci-resolve) all run.

docs.title: README.md checks
docs.text:
When README.md exists, outside fenced code blocks it must have:

  1. exactly one H1 heading,
  2. a ## Table of Contents heading, and
  3. no heading-level skips (for example, ## followed by ####).

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 vergil.toml valid and README.md structure correct 1 vergil.toml invalid or README.md structure incorrect 2 vergil.toml not found

docs.title: getting-started.md (quickstart, one-screen)
docs.text:
Target audience: new consumer, five to ten minutes to a running setup. Structured as eight numbered steps:

  1. Prerequisites (Docker, uv, gh, macOS/Linux)
  2. Clone standard-tooling as a sibling
  3. Bootstrap the host venv with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-host uv sync --group dev
  4. PATH setup for .venv-host/bin and scripts/bin
  5. Git hook configuration
  6. Enable the Claude Code plugin via .claude/settings.json
  7. Create docs/repository-standards.md (minimal example)
  8. Adopt the worktree convention
  9. Verify — three sanity-checks (host bridge, plugin, git hook)

Ends with next-steps links into the full walkthrough, git-workflow guide, and worktree spec.

docs.title: consuming-repo-setup.md (full walkthrough)
docs.text:
Target audience: same new consumer, wants to understand why each step exists and pick up CI + markdownlint + plugin configuration in detail. Structured as ten numbered steps plus mental-model intro, verification protocol, update procedure, and troubleshooting.

Key differences from the old content:

  • Opens with a three-surface mental model (host bridge / dev container / plugin) plus two scripted layers (local git hook + CI composite action) so the reader can orient.
  • The dual-venv rationale (.venv in container vs .venv-host on host) is spelled out where it matters — bootstrapping and keeping up to date. Both point at UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-host and warn against dropping the override.
  • Repository-profile section gets the full attribute-value table and notes values with <, >, | are rejected as placeholders.
  • Plugin section carries an explicit warning pointing at standard-tooling-plugin#46 (release setup) rather than pretending the install flow is smooth.
  • Markdownlint config documents the MD013 tables/code_blocks exemption and the MD060 disable we set in Phase 1.
  • CI section uses the dev-base container image (not the renamed- away dev-docs), matching #252.
  • Troubleshooting section addresses the common new-user failures (.venv-host built wrong, plugin not loaded, worktree commit blocked, auto-merge CalledProcessError from #268).

docs.title: git-workflow.md
docs.text:
Removed the "Setup docs are being refreshed" caveat block that pointed at Phase 2 as future work. Updated the adoption-path section to link both the quickstart and the full walkthrough as explicit entry points.

Dogfooded the worktree convention — work happened in .worktrees/issue-272-onboarding-rewrite/.

  • add git-URL dev-dependency convention spec (#285) Documents the convention that replaces the sibling-checkout plus manual-PATH model for making standard-tooling's host-side CLI tools available in consuming managed repositories.

  • reject git-URL dev-dep approach; add pushback report (#287) The [tool.uv.sources] pattern assumed all consumers are uv-managed Python projects, but only 1 of 5 non-deferred in-scope repos (ARM) has a pyproject.toml. Plugin, docker, and both docs repos have no pyproject.toml and cannot adopt the pattern. The plugin repo specifically was the driver per plugin#69 — the approach cannot solve the problem it was created to solve.

Adds a pushback report at paad/pushback-reviews/ capturing the rejection reasons and the replacement direction (standard-tooling as a host-level developer tool). Marks the spec landed via #285 as superseded so future readers don't rely on it.

Replacement tracked in #286.

  • add host-level-tool spec, plan, pushback, and alignment artifacts (#290) Replaces the rejected git-URL dev-dependency approach (#284, #285, PR #287) with a host-level-tool distribution model. Three coordinated deployment targets — developer host, Python project .venv, and dev container image — share a single source of truth (the rolling v{major.minor} tag).

Artifacts in this PR (no implementation yet):

  • docs/specs/host-level-tool.md — the spec. Six principles, three deployment targets, canonical install via uv tool install, .venv-host retained for dev-tree override, Python consumers MUST declare standard-tooling as a dev dep, dev container images MUST rebuild on each release, git-hook becomes a five-line env-var-plus-GIT_REFLOG_ACTION gate with checks moved into st-commit.

  • docs/plans/host-level-tool-plan.md — seven-phase implementation plan. Phase 1 code work in this repo; Phase 2 cuts v1.3.0; Phase 3 owns standard-tooling-docker#51; Phase 4 owns a new standard-actions issue; Phases 5-6 migrate consumers; Phase 7 is the docs sweep (#288). Phase 1 tasks rewritten in red/green/ refactor TDD format per paad:alignment.

  • paad/pushback-reviews/2026-04-24-host-level-tool-pushback.md — pushback review record. 9 issues found, 8 resolved by spec edits, 1 dismissed (rollback plan; fleet-of-one fail-forward).

  • paad/alignment-reviews/2026-04-25-host-level-tool-alignment.md — alignment review record. 5 issues found, all resolved by plan edits. Plan now covers every spec acceptance criterion; no orphaned tasks.

docs.title: New CLI: st-merge-when-green
docs.text:
Added src/standard_tooling/bin/merge_when_green.py (entry point st-merge-when-green in pyproject.toml). Wraps two gh calls:

gh pr checks --watch --fail-fast gh pr merge -- [--delete-branch]

Default strategy is merge (release/bump PRs use merge commits). Intentionally dumb — on any check failure, exit non-zero and surface the error to the caller. The caller (release skill) owns the "what to do on failure" context; this tool owns the task.

docs.title: Remove auto-merge calls
docs.text:
• st-submit-pr (submit_pr.py): removed the final github.auto_merge() call. The PR gets created; the tool exits. Also fixes #268.
  • st-prepare-release (prepare_release.py): same. Now prints a hint pointing at st-merge-when-green once the PR is live.

docs.title: Prune the dead helper
docs.text:
• refuse feature-branch commits from main worktree (#259) (#275)
  • feat: refuse feature-branch commits from main worktree (#259)

Extends the repo pre-commit hook to enforce rule 3 of the worktree convention: when a .worktrees/ directory is present, commits on feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/, or chore/ branches are refused from the main worktree. This catches out-of-worktree edits that would otherwise slip past the agent-prompt contract.

The opt-in signal is the presence of .worktrees/ at the repo root, so consuming repos that have not yet adopted the convention are unaffected until they do.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• normalize validation stack to one container per run (#282)
  • refactor(validation): normalize validation stack to one container per run

Normalize the validation stack so Docker is invoked exactly once per validation pass, not once per inner script.

docs.title: Before
docs.text: st-validate-local required docker + st-docker-test on PATH. It dispatched to per-language validators which called scripts/dev/{lint,test,typecheck,audit}.sh; each of those scripts re-containerized via st-docker-test. The result was a doubly-containerized invocation that couldn't actually work via st-docker-run -- uv run st-validate-local (docker-in-docker unavailable inside the dev-python container).

docs.title: After
docs.text:
Two clean layers:

  • Outer: st-docker-run launches the dev container once and runs st-validate-local inside it.
  • Inner: scripts/dev/*.sh are tiny, container-local scripts that invoke tooling directly (uv run ruff check, etc.). They do NOT containerize themselves.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• scripts/dev/{lint,test,typecheck,audit}.sh rewritten as simple container-local bash: uv sync, then the actual tool.
  • validate_local_common.py stops launching a container via docker-test; it delegates directly to validate_local_common_container.main() (both modules kept so entry points and tests are minimally disturbed).
  • validate_local.py drops the docker / st-docker-test precondition check — st-validate-local now expects to run inside a container, and a caller who mis-runs it on the host will get clear errors from the inner scripts about missing uv/ruff/etc.
  • Tests updated to match the simplified control flow.
  • CLAUDE.md "Three-Tier CI Model" and "Docker-First Testing" sections rewritten to reflect the new single-container design. The scripts/dev/*.sh files are now documented as the per-repo customization point.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• st-docker-run -- uv run pytest tests/ ... passes all 420 tests with 100% coverage.
  • Direct invocation from a worktree crashed at git.repo_root() inside the container because the worktree's .git file points at an absolute host path not mounted inside. Filed as #281; not caused by this PR and orthogonal to its scope.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This PR normalizes this repo only. Parallel work tracked in other tooling repos (standard-actions, standard-tooling-plugin, standard-tooling-docker, standards-and-conventions, infrastructure-mindset, ai-research-methodology) per #280. mq-rest-admin-* repos get tracking issues but no code change yet (they're not under active development).

  • consolidate pre-commit checks into st-commit; add env-var gate (#292)
  • refactor(commit): consolidate pre-commit checks into st-commit; add env-var gate

Implements Phase 1 of the host-level-tool plan (docs/plans/host-level-tool-plan.md). Closes #291.

Code changes: - src/standard_tooling/bin/commit.py: ports the five branch / context checks (detached HEAD, protected branches, branch prefix, issue number, worktree convention) verbatim from the now-deleted pre_commit_hook.py. Sets ST_COMMIT_CONTEXT=1 before invoking git commit --file so the new gate admits the commit. - src/standard_tooling/bin/pre_commit_hook.py: deleted. - pyproject.toml: removes the st-pre-commit-hook console-script entry point. Strict semver would warrant v2.0.0; in practice no in-fleet consumer invokes the entry point directly (all wire core.hooksPath at scripts/lib/git-hooks/pre-commit, also deleted here). Release notes for v1.3.0 will call out the removal as a clean break. - scripts/lib/git-hooks/pre-commit: deleted. - .githooks/pre-commit: new env-var-plus-GIT_REFLOG_ACTION gate. Admits ST_COMMIT_CONTEXT=1, admits derived workflows (amend, cherry-pick, revert, rebase, merge), rejects raw git commit. - CLAUDE.md, README.md: updated to reference .githooks/, host-level install model, and the new gate semantics. Stale scripts/bin/ bash-validators section removed (those tools have been Python entry points since #216).

Test changes: - tests/standard_tooling/test_commit.py: 21 new tests pinning the five validation checks (one rejection + one happy path each, plus edge cases) and the ST_COMMIT_CONTEXT=1 env-var contract. Two pre-existing tests adjusted to mock current_branch / is_main_worktree now that validation runs in commit.main(). - tests/standard_tooling/test_pre_commit_hook.py: deleted (logic migrated; coverage preserved by the new tests in test_commit.py). - tests/standard_tooling/test_pre_commit_gate.py: 14 new subprocess tests pinning the gate's three branches (admit-by-env, admit-by-GIT_REFLOG_ACTION across the five admitted patterns, reject for everything else; plus precedence and value-narrowness cases).

All 432 tests pass; 100% coverage maintained.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• regenerate v1.3.0 release notes with correct content st-prepare-release rendered v1.2.2 content into releases/v1.3.0.md because git-cliff's --latest flag falls back to the previous tag's section when the target tag (develop-v1.3.0) doesn't exist yet at release-prep time. CHANGELOG.md is unaffected (no --latest used).

Manual regeneration with --unreleased instead of --latest produces the correct v1.3.0 section. Bug to be tracked in a follow-up issue; the fix in prepare_release.py is a one-flag change.

  • use --unreleased instead of --latest for release notes (#298)

  • remove dead skip-filter from _find_yaml_files Coverage gate caught it: the explicit filter for vendored subtrees was unreachable because discovery only walks .github, docs/site/mkdocs.yml, and repo_root — none of which recurse into .worktrees / .venv / .venv-host / node_modules. The exclusion is structural, not policy. Filter and _YAML_SKIP_DIRS constant removed; the skip test renamed/clarified to pin the structural exclusion.

  • move Path import into TYPE_CHECKING block (TC003) After removing the dead skip-filter, Path is only used as a type annotation (with from future import annotations active). ruff TC003 flags this — moved into the TYPE_CHECKING block.

  • use reference-style links to satisfy markdownlint and lint CI surfaced two issues in the parent commit: a 101-char line in test_finalize_repo.py and 127-char lines in the docs files where I'd inlined the new GitHub blob URLs. Both fix together by switching the long URLs to markdown reference-style links ([text][ref] / [ref]: url) and wrapping the test return_value across two lines. No semantic change.

  • add S607 noqa for gh CLI invocation ruff S607 (partial executable path) flagged the gh invocation in _check_docs_workflow_status. The existing # noqa: S603 already suppresses subprocess shell-injection warnings; adding S607 to that list is the same pattern used elsewhere (test_pre_commit_gate, etc.) for bare-name CLI tools whose absolute path varies by host.

  • use shutil.which to get gh absolute path (S607) Same noqa-attribution pattern as PR #292's bash invocation: newer ruff flags the argument-list line, not the subprocess.run call line, so the # noqa: S607 doesn't suppress. Switching to shutil.which('gh') for the path resolves the warning entirely. Tests pass.

  • use 'git branch -D' for already-vetted merged branches (#307)

docs.text:
• declare GPL-3.0-only license metadata in pyproject.toml Adds [project].license and [project].license-files to pyproject.toml so pip-licenses reports standard-tooling correctly instead of UNKNOWN.

The repo has carried a GPL-3.0 LICENSE file all along; the metadata gap was invisible until ai-research-methodology declared standard-tooling as a dev dep (per the host-level-tool spec) and pip-licenses scanned it. Without this fix every Python consumer of standard-tooling needs a tactical --ignore-packages standard-tooling in audit.sh.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• replace docker info with docker version for daemon reachability check docker info queries full daemon state (storage drivers, plugins, container counts) and can fail or time out even when the daemon is reachable — producing false-positive 'Docker is not available' errors during st-finalize-repo post-finalization validation.

docker version performs a lightweight API version handshake and is the standard reachability check. Also bumps the timeout from 10s to 15s to accommodate slower Docker Desktop VM wake-ups on macOS.

Applied to both assert_docker_available() in lib/docker.py and the parallel _docker_is_available() in docker_test.py.

  • auto-chdir to main worktree instead of erroring from a secondary worktree st-finalize-repo errored when run from inside a .worktrees/ secondary worktree, telling the user to cd to the main worktree manually. This is a trivially correctable situation — the main worktree path is always discoverable via git rev-parse --git-common-dir.

Now detects the secondary worktree, resolves the main worktree root via the new git.main_worktree_root() helper, chdirs there, and continues with a one-line note.

  • skip --delete-branch when running from a secondary worktree gh pr merge --delete-branch attempts to switch the local checkout back to the default branch after deleting the remote branch. This fails when the default branch is already checked out in the main worktree, causing a non-zero exit even though the merge itself succeeded.

When running from a secondary worktree, skip --delete-branch and let st-finalize-repo handle branch and worktree cleanup as usual.

  • bump stale standard-actions pins from @v1.1 to @v1.3 Three standard-actions references were still pinned to @v1.1 while the rest of the fleet is on @v1.3: version-divergence in ci.yml, tag-and-release and version-bump-pr in publish.yml. Bumped all three to @v1.3.

docs.text:
• add post-publish workflow to verify dev container images carry the released version After publish.yml completes, a new verify-docker-images workflow polls dev-base:latest for up to ~25 minutes (13 attempts, 2-minute intervals) to confirm it carries the just-released standard-tooling version.

If the image still carries a stale version after the wait window, the workflow fails and opens (or comments on) a bug issue with next-step instructions.

This catches the silent-staleness scenario from standard-tooling-docker#67 where the fleet ran a 6-week-old standard-tooling version because the image rebuild failed without anyone noticing.
