docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• patient, heartbeating handshake waits; audit acks from state (#1573)
  • fix(pr-workflow): make the agent handshake waits patient and heartbeating (#1572)

The audit's bootstrap wait used a 30s timeout, so it failed before the implement session was ready; and a long silent block reads as a hang. Make all agent-to-agent waits use the long timeout and emit a periodic stderr heartbeat naming what they wait on, so the watching human sees the loop is alive (transparency is the oversight model). Threads an optional waiting_for through the Transport ABC and the local transport.

  • fix(pr-workflow): let the audit ack from state so it needs no issue number (#1572)

The audit is launched against the worktree path the implement session hands off, so it should not require --issue. Take the issue from the workflow state when --issue is omitted; update the e2e test to assert the audit acks and gets a review directive rather than erroring.

  • test(pr-workflow): stop the suite sleeping/hanging on real-time waits (#1572)

The oracle's poll interval (1s) and patient timeout (24h) are now env-overridable and read at call time; a pr_workflow conftest fixture sets a 0 poll and a short timeout so CLI-driven waits never sleep on real time. Previously any test that hit a wait which did not resolve on the first read blocked for the timeout — seconds each, or an effective hang under the patient timeout — pushing the suite past 30 minutes. The full suite now runs in ~4.5s. Also reseed the audit-next-without-issue e2e test so its wait resolves, and cover the ack-from-state path at the orchestration level.

  • chore(pr-workflow): remove scratch timing files accidentally committed (#1572)

Drop .dur.txt and .prw.txt, throwaway pytest-timing captures that should never have been staged.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• report GitHub API failures as named errors instead of a traceback (#3208) vrg-pr-await now catches GitHubAPIError around wait_for_settle. A permission failure (HTTP 403 / Resource not accessible by integration on the checks or Actions reads) is reported as a GitHub App permissions problem for the PR's owner/repo, pointing at the Checks and Actions read permissions. Any other API failure is printed plainly with its gh output, and a missing token uses the shared missing-token message. All exit 1; the underlying gh error text is always shown. Ref #2862

  • link ci-sync tasks per-org and discard the probe worktree on failure (#3209) vrg-ci-sync hardcoded the vergil-project epic, so vrg-issue-create refused every repo in another org as a cross-org link. It now passes epic=None, linking each repo under its own org's ad-hoc epic, matching vrg-fleet-sync and vrg-xdist-sync.

The fleet-sweep driver stranded .worktrees/probe- when a repo failed before the probe was renamed, so the next sweep of that repo failed at worktree add. A failure in the probe phase now removes the probe; if that removal fails too, the error names both failures. A worktree already renamed to issue-- is never removed.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• add routine App private key rotation procedure (#3210) Add a Rotating an App private key section to credential-management.md covering the user and audit agent Apps: generate a second key, repoint private_key_path in identities.toml, re-inject via vrg-vm restart (Lima) or vrg-vm rebuild (off-platform), verify with a token-minting vrg-gh read, then delete the old key. Repoint the compromise-response Restore step at the new section instead of issue #779. The classic-PAT half of #779 is obsolete; agents no longer use PATs.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• fail loudly when App token minting fails instead of falling back to ambient gh auth (#3219) When App credentials are configured, a failure to mint an installation token (JWT signing, installation lookup, token exchange, malformed or tokenless response) now raises AppAuthError carrying the underlying detail instead of logging a warning and returning None. None meant ambient gh auth, so an agent with a broken key on a host with a human gh login silently acted as the human. AppAuthError is deliberately not a CalledProcessError so gh-failure handlers cannot swallow it; an import-time sys.excepthook in lib/github prints it as an actionable message (exit 1, no traceback) from every entry point, and vrg-gh catches it explicitly. No App config is unchanged. The no-installation path for cwd-scoped callers keeps its ambient fallback (deliberately relied on since #2070) but now warns once per owner. The key-rotation verify step in credential-management.md describes the new behaviour. Refs #3214

  • fail loudly when App mode is configured but no target org can be determined (#3222)

  • fix(github): fail loudly when App mode is configured but no target org can be determined

When GitHub App credentials are configured and no org is given or detectable from the cwd origin remote, get_installation_token now raises NoTargetOrgError (an AppAuthError subclass) instead of returning None, which let gh/git silently use ambient auth. Without App config the no-org path still returns None (human-mode ambient auth). detect_org also recognises ssh://git@github.com/ remotes. Docs describe the no-org failure.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• put main() first in every bin/ module (#3218) Move main() to be the first top-level function in each src/vergil_tooling/bin module, with parse_args/_parse_args immediately after it. Pure reordering of top-level definitions: no function bodies, names, signatures or docstrings changed, and the main guard stays at the bottom. Update the CLI entry-point standard to main-first and add an ast-based test that keeps main as the first function in every bin/ module. Ref #3199

  • replace the import-time sys.excepthook with a cli_main boundary on every entry point (#3221) lib/github.py no longer installs a global sys.excepthook at import time. A new lib/cli.py provides the cli_main decorator, applied to the main() of every [project.scripts] entry point: AppAuthError, NoInstallationError and MissingGitHubTokenError that escape main are printed as ': ' on stderr with exit status 1; every other exception propagates unchanged, and handlers already inside main keep their command-specific messages. lib.github is imported lazily on the failure path so commands that never reach GitHub (vrg-hook-guard) pay no import cost. A structural test enforces the decorator on every console script, and the #3214 subprocess test now runs vrg-roadmap end to end against a broken App key.

    CI Evidence: All gates passed — full audit bundle available. Download →

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• scope vrg-docs-stage, vrg-ci-evidence and vrg-github-repo-config tokens to their --repo owner (#3228) Each command now runs its GitHub calls under github.target_org(), so the App installation token is minted for the target repo rather than the cwd org. When --repo is omitted (vrg-docs-stage, vrg-github-repo-config) the cwd repo is resolved first and its owner scopes the token, as before.

    Under target_org a missing App installation for the owner raises NoInstallationError instead of the warn-and-fallback to ambient auth, matching every other target_org command. vrg-docs-stage and vrg-ci-evidence report it through cli_main (exit 1). vrg-github-repo-config reports it, and any AppAuthError, as exit 2 (audit could not complete), so vrg-release preflight no longer misreads an auth failure as non-compliance; a non-404 API error while resolving vergil.toml is now exit 2 as well instead of escaping.

    vrg-ci-evidence harvest/bundle also read the release PR head with a bare PR number, which gh resolves against the cwd repo; it now passes the PR URL for --repo.

    Tests use a new fake_app fixture that runs the real token selection against fake installations, covering --repo from outside a repo, from a different-org repo, and an uninstalled owner. The credential-management guide names --repo as an explicit target.

    • read the --repo target's vergil.toml at the release PR head in harvest (#3229)
    • fix(ci-evidence): read the --repo target's vergil.toml at the release PR head in harvest

    harvest (and bundle, which composes it) derived the required evidence gates from the vergil.toml in the current directory. Outside a checkout it failed; from another repo's checkout it silently judged the target's checks against the wrong config.

    resolve_required_gates now fetches the --repo target's vergil.toml through the contents API at the release PR's validated head SHA, the commit whose CI run is being evidenced, so the required set matches that run from any directory. An absent or unparseable file raises RemoteConfigError, reported as a one-line error with no cwd fallback. Only Contents: read is needed.

    The contents-API helpers move from vrg-github-repo-config into a new lib/remote_config module so both commands share them; vrg-github-repo-config keeps its develop-then-cwd resolution unchanged.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• document the Actions, Checks and Commit statuses read grants on both agent Apps (#3227) vrg-pr-await and pr-watch read a PR's check runs, commit statuses and workflow runs. On a private repo an App without these read-only grants gets HTTP 403 "Resource not accessible by integration"; on public repos the reads succeed anyway, which hid the gap. Both Apps now hold the three grants. The account-setup permission tables, the setup checklist and the identity-architecture capability lists now say so, and vrg-pr-await's 403 hint names Commit statuses as well.

  • document vrg-host and the host dependency pinning workflow (#3262) Add a vrg-host reference page (subcommands, severities and exit codes, the packaged manifest and what is in and out of it, the gcloud numpy check, user-config pins with the #155 doctrine, constraint grammar, re-evaluation, no privilege escalation) and wire it into the site nav, the script reference, the CLI tools overview, getting started, consuming-repo setup, releasing, the VM spec, README and CLAUDE.md. Ref #2450.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add host-dependency manifest schema and TOML loader (#3243) Add vergil_tooling.lib.host_deps (HostDependency, AuxCheck, HostPin, ManifestError, load_manifest) and a minimal packaged host_dependencies.toml seed (uv, gh). The manifest is read only from vergil_tooling.data via importlib.resources and parsed with stdlib tomllib; unknown enums, missing or mistyped fields, unknown keys, duplicates, and a pin without a reason all raise ManifestError. Ship data/*.toml as package data. Ref #2451

  • add install-method handler registry (#3244) Add host_methods: installed_version/latest_version/upgrade dispatching on brew-formula, brew-cask, uv-tool and custom, behind a single stubbable _run seam. UNMANAGED sentinel distinguishes a declared no-feed latest from a failed probe (None). upgrade raises UpgradeUnsupported(Error) for manual deps and UpgradeFailedError when the command fails; unknown methods and missing custom probes raise ManifestError. _run refuses privilege escalators and closes stdin so nothing prompts for a password. Ref #2452

  • add vrg-host status with two-axis classification (#3246)

  • feat(host): add vrg-host status with two-axis classification

Adds lib/host_status.py (classify version state x auxiliary checks, worst-severity roll-up, latest-unmanaged OK/info vs latest-unknown WARN, render) and bin/vrg_host.py with the status subcommand (default when bare; exit code = worst severity). A probe whose output cannot be parsed, an unprobeable manifest entry, or a privilege-refused probe is reported per dependency as an explicit probe-error (ERROR) without aborting the rest of the report. Registers vrg-host in [project.scripts]. Ref #2453.

  • fix(host): compare active pins by version-prefix constraint, not string equality

Adds host_status.pin_satisfied: a pin constraint is a dotted version prefix with optional trailing 'x' wildcards (1.x, 2.40.x, or an exact 2.40.0); trailing x components are dropped and the rest must equal the installed version's leading components. Any other syntax (<=, >=, ~=, empty or non-trailing-x components) raises ValueError. classify reports an active pin as pinned/OK when satisfied and pinned/WARN when drifted; vrg-host status routes an unsupported constraint to that dependency's probe-error (ERROR) line. Ref #2453.

  • add vrg-host pin/unpin with #155 lifecycle surfacing (#3247) Pins live in the host-local ~/.config/vergil/host-pins.toml (beside identities.toml), never in the packaged manifest, and are overlaid onto it at load time so status sees the merged view. The pins file can only hold back declared dependencies; malformed files, undeclared or reason-less pins are loud errors. pin validates the constraint grammar up front; unpin sets state to freed and keeps the record as history. status renders active pins as tracked debt (constraint, latest held back from, reason, tracking issue, age) and raises a re-evaluation-due or re-evaluation-unknown pin to WARN.

  • add auxiliary-check remediation and gcloud numpy check (#3248)

  • feat(host): add auxiliary-check remediation and gcloud numpy check

Add remediate_checks(dep), which runs the remediation of each unsatisfied auxiliary check through the unprivileged _run seam and re-probes to verify it; a failed or ineffective remediation raises RemediationFailedError. Wire it into a new 'vrg-host status --fix' flag, which skips missing dependencies, reports failures on stderr and forces exit 2. Add the gcloud custom manifest entry with the numpy-in-interpreter check (absorbs vergil-project/.github#166).

  • add vrg-host upgrade (auto/manual, pin-respecting, no escalation) (#3249) Upgrades only upgrade=auto deps (named or --all). Named manual deps are refused (exit 1); --all lists every manual dep it skipped. An active pin holds the dep unless --force; an unsupported pin constraint is an error for that dep. Upgrade failures and privilege-escalation refusals are reported per dep as needing manual action, never retried elevated, and set exit 2. Ref #2455.

  • enumerate and curate the host-dependency manifest (#3250)

  • feat(host): enumerate and curate the host-dependency manifest

Curate the full macOS host manifest (plan Task 7, spec §4/§11): uv (custom, standalone installer), gh, gcloud, lima, docker (manual, unmanaged latest; Docker Desktop today), opentofu, git-cliff, vergil-tooling (uv-tool, unmanaged latest since it is git-sourced) and macos (manual, softwareupdate probe). Container-only linters, az, git/jq and personal tools are recorded as out of scope.

Add host_versions as the single normalizer and comparator: handlers return bare versions (gh version 2.40.0 == 2.40.0), status orders them so an install newer than latest is current, brew revisions compare, and an unorderable pair raises instead of guessing. host_pins now uses it for the #155 trigger.

Harden the brew/uv/custom parsers (newest keg, formula revision, --formula disambiguation, unreadable answers are probe errors) against probe-output fixtures that were constructed from documented formats, not captured on a Mac; the fixtures README lists them for re-capture.

  • add held-back report, [dependency-update] config and the repo-hook updater (#3263)
  • keep failed dependency updates open as labelled PRs with a fix task (#3265)
  • report direct Python dependencies held back by their declared bounds (#3266)
  • normalize action.yml refs and bump the vergil-python runtime from every serving index (#3267)
  • feat(update-deps): normalize action.yml refs and bump the vergil-python runtime from every serving index

A [package.python] runtime pin is bumped to the newest patch on its minor line that every index the release reads it from serves: the shared deb suite for both arches plus every selected target (deb by suite/arch, rpm by suite/rpm_arch). A newer served minor is reported as held back. Index lookup failures fail loud as UpdateDepsError. normalize_refs now also rewrites composite action.yml/action.yaml files. package_index gains deb_package_names/rpm_package_names on top of extracted _stanzas/_rpm_primary helpers (deb_has/rpm_has unchanged in behaviour).

  • style(update-deps): apply ruff formatting to the runtime-bump changes

  • add the images updater: bump exact tags within their major, report newer series (#3268)

  • run the dependency update as the last vrg-release stage (#3270) Adds the update-deps stage (fail_defer) between consumer-refresh and publish-status. It fast-forwards the root develop checkout and runs the vrg-update-deps pipeline via run_update(). The tracking comment carries the held-back report and the PR link; a recorded failure is raised so the tracking issue gets the failure comment, and publish-status repeats it alongside any deferred publish failure. --without-deps skips the stage.

  • fold live macOS captures into the probe fixtures and correct uv/Docker install methods (#3271) Replace the constructed vrg-host probe fixtures with output captured on a real macOS host (2026-10-16), keeping only the cases the host could not produce as labelled constructed fixtures. Add an end-to-end status test that replays the captures through stub host tools and checks unchanged rows against the real vrg-host status output.

Manifest changes verified on the host: - uv is Homebrew-installed (no uv self update): method brew-formula, latest is Homebrew stable. - docker -> docker-desktop: a brew-cask entry whose installed version comes from the app's Info.plist (Desktop self-updates, so Homebrew's record goes stale); latest from the docker-desktop cask; upgrade stays manual. - gcloud stays custom (its component manager owns updates); its why warns never to brew upgrade --greedy it.

  • gate vrg-release on open dependency-update PRs, with --allow-pending-deps (#3272) A fresh vrg-release preflight now refuses while any open PR carries the dependency-update label, naming each PR and its fix task and how to clear the gate. --allow-pending-deps bypasses it for urgent releases; the bypassed PRs are recorded on the release context and named in the prepare-stage tracking comment. The gate is skipped on --resume. A failed or malformed PR lookup raises ReleaseError rather than passing silently. Ref vergil-tooling issue 3258, epic vergil-project/.github#381, spec section 5.3.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• derive the vergil series for new-repo templates from the installed tooling (#3264) default_vergil_series() returns vX.Y of the installed vergil-tooling. docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• land 2.1.244 dependency update with ty 0.0.89 typing fixes (#3284)

  • chore(deps): uv lock --upgrade

  • fix(deps): make ty 0.0.89 typecheck clean

The uv lock --upgrade in #3281 moved ty from 0.0.38 to 0.0.89, which reports new errors and deprecation warnings. Annotate the comprehension-built versions lists in test_repo_init as list[str]; swap NamedTemporaryFile.write in test_release_tracking via monkeypatch.setattr instead of attribute assignment (dropping the mypy ignore); and annotate @contextmanager functions as Generator[X] rather than the deprecated Iterator[X]. No behaviour change. Ref #3282

  • carry the failing validation stage's output, count a deps-only failure once (#3285)
  • fix(update-deps): carry the failing validation stage's output in a deps failure

A validation failure now shows the output of the vrg-validate stage(s) that failed, isolated from vrg-validate's stdout by its stage markers and followed by its summary, instead of the raw tail of the whole run (#3283). When no failing stage can be isolated, the raw tail is shown under a heading that says so. An empty output renders as an explicit placeholder. The size bounds are unchanged.

  • fix(release): count a deps-only failure once in the release summary

When the dependency update fails and no CD publish was deferred, publish-status now repeats the deps failure as a warning on its own row instead of raising a second failure, so the summary reads one failed stage (update-deps) while the warnings list still carries the deps failure (#3283). With a deferred publish it still raises, carrying both messages.

  • close a dependency-update PR at preflight once its fix task completes (#3287) A squash-merged fix PR never marks the dependency-update PR merged, so the release gate stayed shut after the fix landed (#3281/#3282/#3284). Preflight now looks up each open deps PR's fix task: closed as COMPLETED -> comment and close the PR, record it on the release context, and name it in the prepare-stage tracking comment. Closed for any other reason, open, or missing keeps blocking (non-completed closure gets its own refusal text). All fix tasks are looked up before any PR is closed; lookup, comment and close failures raise ReleaseError naming the PR's state. --allow-pending-deps applies only to what still blocks; --resume still skips the check. Also corrects the fix-task body, which claimed GitHub marks the deps PR merged.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• track git, bash, Xcode Command Line Tools and Claude Code (#3302) Add four host dependencies the vrg-host manifest missed.

  • git and bash: brew-formula, auto. On a Homebrew-first Mac both resolve to Homebrew ahead of the Apple copies, so they are no longer in the deliberately-out list.

  • xcode-clt: custom, manual (report-only, like macos). Installed from pkgutil CLTools_Executables, keeping the first three components (26.6.0.0.1781586589 reads as 26.6.0) so it compares with Software Update's Version. Latest parses the Command Line Tools items of softwareupdate --list (latest_versions); none listed means current; an unreadable item or pkgutil answer is a probe error. Missing CLT is ERROR.
  • claude-code: brew-cask, auto. The cask does not declare auto_updates (Homebrew API, 2026-10-16), reversing the #167 spec's personal-tool exclusion because it is the host-side agent for out-of-sandbox work.

Adds recorded and constructed fixtures (labelled in the fixtures README), tests, and updates the vrg-host reference and getting-started docs.

  • skip current dependencies and report before -> after versions in vrg-host upgrade (#3303) vrg-host upgrade now probes and classifies each auto dependency as status does before acting. A current dependency is skipped without running its upgrade command. A behind dependency is upgraded and its installed version is re-probed, so the line reports the real before -> after; an upgrade that leaves the version unchanged is WARN, never 'upgraded'. Dependencies with no latest feed run and report before -> after; missing or probe-error dependencies are ERROR and not attempted. Held lines now show the installed version and the latest held back from. The --all hold exemption from the exit-code roll-up now applies only to pin holds.

• refuse to release a package version an earlier release already published (#3311) Package builds are not byte-reproducible, so rebuilding a published (name, full version, arch, format) breaks the shared package index for every repo. vrg-release preflight now refuses such a release on a fresh start, before anything is tagged, and vrg-package check-unpublished offers the same check as a CD backstop. Both reuse the index's identity and release-collection logic and fail closed when the published state cannot be read.

• report a CD watch timeout as result-unknown and name both batch post-checks (#3317) The CD watch deadline was a fixed 1800s, below vergil-containers' routine ~43m CD (run 38973347564 took 43m31s), and a timeout was reported with the same headline as a failed run. The default is now 5400s (90 min, about 2x the longest known CD), overridable with VRG_CD_TIMEOUT, validated like VRG_CHECKS_TIMEOUT (a malformed value raises). A timeout gets its own headline (still in progress after Ns; result unknown) with the run URL and re-check instructions, and still fails the stage.

The end-of-batch vrg-finalize-pr --cleanup-only runs validation and the CD check, but every batch labelled a non-zero exit as validation. The shared post-step is now named post-checks and says 'end-of-batch post-checks (validation + CD check)', defined once in lib/pr_workflow/batch.py for all three batch paths.

• probe xdist in the project test env and make the worker count tunable per context (#3323) vrg-validate probed pytest-xdist with its own interpreter (the uv tool venv), so consumer repos never got the parallel flags. The probe now runs at test-stage time, after install, against the interpreter beside the pytest on PATH (.venv/bin first). A probe that cannot run, or errors, fails the stage instead of degrading to serial.

The xdist worker count is now tunable: [test].workers ("auto" or a positive int) is the repo default, [test.].workers overrides it for one validation context (ci, local-vm, cloud-vm, physical-host), and VRG_TEST_WORKERS overrides both on one machine. vrg-container-run resolves the context outside the container (GITHUB_ACTIONS, else vrg-whoami --platform) and forwards it as VRG_TEST_CONTEXT. The test stage prints its parallelism decision and where the count came from.

docs.text:
• offer "none of the above" for primary-language (#1580) The init wizard forced a primary-language choice among the five languages with no way to express a language-less repo, so adopting a repo like .github (documentation, no language) could only be escaped with Ctrl-C.

Pull primary-language out of the generic required-enum loop and give it its own prompt with a separate "0. None of the above" option, set apart from the real languages. Selecting it maps to an empty string so render_vergil_toml omits the primary-language key entirely, which the config parser and vrg-validate already treat as a valid language-less repo. The five-language enum, the on-disk omission model, and the lack of any default are all unchanged.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: <ul> <li>delete the branch when the dependency-update gate closes a PR (#3338) GitHub's delete-on-merge setting never applies to a PR closed without merging, so the gate's auto-close of a landed dependency-update PR left deps/update- on origin indefinitely (vergil-tooling deps/update-2.1.244, vergil-vm deps/update-2.1.44). Preflight now deletes the head branch after closing the PR. The delete is a separate step rather than gh pr close --delete-branch, because gh exits non-zero when the close succeeds but the delete fails, which the close handler would misreport as the PR still being open. An already-deleted branch counts as deleted. Any other failure prints a warning with the manual command and is named in the prepare comment on the tracking issue; the gate still clears because the PR is closed. A test now requires every gh pr close in src/ to pass --delete-branch or say why not. Ref #3332

Keeps the default branch, develop, main, gh-pages, protected branches (branches API flag plus any ruleset rule from the rules-for-branch endpoint), no-PR branches and reused branch names. Per-branch errors are reported and the run exits non-zero after processing the rest. Safety net behind delete-on-merge and the delete-on-close rule (#3332).

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• update instead of aborting on stale failed checks when BEHIND (#3359) The failed-checks gate in wait_and_merge ran before the post-wait BEHIND recheck. When the lazily-computed mergeStateStatus missed a freshly-behind branch at the loop-top precheck, wait() returned at once on the already terminal (stale) checks and a stale red check hard-aborted the merge, never reaching the update-and-retry path from #2856.

Before aborting on failed checks, re-check BEHIND; if the branch is behind, update it via _update_or_abort() (update-branch cancels the stale runs and starts fresh ones) and loop, bounded by the shared _MAX_BRANCH_UPDATES cap. A failure on a current branch still aborts.

  • pin confirm-develop to the back-merge commit, not the develop tip (#3360) confirm-develop polled for the CD run of the current origin/develop tip. On vrg-release --resume the tip can have moved (a dependency-update or feature PR merged after the back-merge), so the stage verified, or waited on and failed over, a run unrelated to the release.

back-merge-bump now records the back-merge PR's merge commit (mergeCommit.oid via github.merge_commit_sha) on ReleaseContext on every path: create, adopt-open and adopt-merged. The context is not persisted; a resume re-runs back-merge-bump, which adopts the PR and records the SHA again. confirm-develop polls for that SHA's run and fails loudly when none was recorded, with no fallback to the tip. confirm-main is unchanged.

close-finalize now runs vrg-finalize-pr with --no-wait-cd. Its cleanup-only cd-check has no merge to pin to and would watch the develop tip, with the same problem. confirm-develop has already verified the right run, finalize is reached only when it passed, and the second wait would also re-fail on a docs failure confirm-develop deferred. Documented in the release guide.

  • resolve a leftover deps/update branch by its PR state instead of refusing (#3363) vrg-update-deps preflight refused whenever deps/update- existed locally or on origin, treating it as in flight. A branch can outlive its PR: GitHub's delete-on-merge never applies to a PR closed without merging, and occasionally skips its after-merge processing. A re-run at the same version, including the update-deps stage of vrg-release --resume, then failed even though nothing was in flight.

    Preflight now looks up the branch's PRs (the vrg-branch-sweep helpers). If the newest PR merged, the update for that version is done: preflight reports it and the run exits 0 without updating, and the vrg-release update-deps stage records it as done rather than failed. If it was closed without merging, the stale branch is deleted on origin and locally, by name, and the update runs. An open PR, no PR, an unexpected state, or a tip that is not the last PR's head still refuses as in flight.

    After merging its PR, the merge stage now deletes the branch on origin as its own API step (already-deleted is fine; a failure warns without failing the run). It does not pass gh pr merge --delete-branch: github.merge is shared, and gh would also try to switch the linked worktree off the branch, which can fail after a successful merge.

    • fail loudly when scripts/bin/validate-custom is not executable (#3364) _find_custom_validator only returned scripts/bin/validate-custom when it was an executable regular file, so a script that lost its executable bit was treated exactly like an absent one: the custom stage vanished and vrg-validate reported green without running the repo's own gates.

    Discovery now returns anything present at that path, and the custom stage checks it first (_check_custom_validator), failing with the path and the fix (chmod +x and commit the mode change) when it is not executable or not a regular file. An absent script is still a no-op.

    • stop reporting a stale in_progress CD job as a failed publish (#3366) Releasing vergil-vm v2.1.47, every step of release / package-matrix ran but the jobs API kept reporting it in_progress with a null conclusion after the run concluded success. _collect_deferred_publish counted the null conclusion as a failure and collapsed it to its family, so vrg-release reported 'CD publish jobs did not succeed: release', held the consumer refresh and left the tracking issue open for a fully delivered release.

    • The settle wait now waits, within the same bounded budget, for every job to reach completed, not only the release (or docs) job.

    • Only completed jobs are judged as failed. A job still non-terminal after the budget is checked against the run-level conclusion: under success the record is stale, reported by name as a warning and never deferred; under any other conclusion it is deferred as ' (never settled)'.
    • A failed job in the release job's own family is reported by its full name, so the message cannot read as the release itself failing.
    • One combined stage warning, since mark_warn is last-call-wins.

    • The release guide documents stale job records.

    • detect stale check-runs while waiting, not only at the deadline (#3374)

    • fix(github): detect stale check-runs while waiting, not only at the deadline

      • wait_for_checks now probes each pending Actions check's backing run (throttled to every 30s per run). A check still pending 60s after its run completed is decided by the backing job's own conclusion: success passes it with a named warning; any other or unreadable conclusion raises OrphanedCheckError at once. The deadline stays the backstop. Ref #3358

      • docs(finalize-pr): document in-wait stale check-run detection

      • ensure issue labels exist at the point of use (#3378) vrg-triage-create and vrg-issue-create now create every label they apply in the target repo, from data/labels.json, before creating the issue, so a repo that was never label-synced no longer fails with '' not found. One shared helper, labels.ensure_labels, replaces the copies in epics.py and update_deps/pr.py. A label missing from the registry is refused with an actionable error and nothing is created; a failing gh label create stops the command with the gh detail and no issue is created. Ref #3373

      • resolve the Conan audit token from its file at point of use (#3380) vrg-container-run now resolves CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER itself for cpp repos instead of relying on the ambient environment, which only an interactive bash sourcing ~/.bashrc populated. Precedence: a non-blank env var wins, then ~/.config/vergil/conan.env, then the conan_audit_token_path file in identities.toml. A source that exists but is unreadable, malformed or empty fails loudly; no token at all keeps the #2895 skip. The value reaches the runtime through its environment and is forwarded by name, so it never appears in argv. Consuming repos no longer need a [container].env-prefixes entry for it. The ~/.bashrc source line stays as a convenience for manual conan use. Ref #2902

      • fail fast on a stale check-run that is a required status check (#3383)

      • fix(github): fail fast on a stale check-run that is a required status check

        • A stale check over a successful job is passed only when it is not required by the base branch. A required one, or one seen while the required set could not be read, raises OrphanedCheckError at once, since GitHub keeps blocking the merge on it. pr_merge passes the required-check lookup result through unchanged (None = unknown) instead of coercing it to an empty set, and its orphan abort now carries the waiter's detail. The normal wait path keeps the #3061 fallback. Ref #3379

        • docs(finalize-pr): document fail-fast for stale required check-runs

        • drop the deprecated run-standards input and stale CI, scripts/dev and deps/ guidance (#3389) render_ci_workflow no longer passes run-standards to ci-security.yml, which documents it as deprecated and ignored. CLAUDE.md drops the retired standards-compliance PR-CI gate and the scripts/dev/test.sh wrapper, and describes how vrg-container-test picks its language. The obsolete Python local-validation-scripts page (scripts/dev/validate_local.py) is removed. git-workflow.md now states that vrg-commit refuses deps/update- by design, because vrg-update-deps commits there with git directly. Ref #3384

        • name the publish credentials the tools actually read (#3395) Rust now names CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, which cargo publish reads and the registry-publish action sets, instead of CRATES_IO_TOKEN. Python names no credential (None), matching Go: it publishes through PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC), and nothing ever set PYPI_TOKEN. vrg-ecosystem-resolve output changes accordingly. Ref #3394.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• make the .claude/settings.json attribution audit strict (#3376) A missing or different attribution value in .claude/settings.json is now a local.claude_settings.attribution DiffItem instead of a warning. The expected value names the required key and #3200. There is no exemption for dormant repos: one whose nightly audit still runs fails until it adds the key. Ref #3361.

  • show every worktree in the repo, grouped by kind (#3390)

  • feat(worktree-status): show every worktree in the repo, grouped by kind, and flag the main checkout

vrg-worktree-status now lists the main checkout and every linked worktree git knows about, in four sections: main checkout, development (feature/-), release and dependency machinery (release/, deps/update-), and other/unknown (any other branch, a detached HEAD, or a worktree outside .worktrees/). The main checkout is flagged when it is off the integration branch from the branching model in vergil.toml (develop when there is no vergil.toml), dirty, or mid-rebase. A branch deleted on its remote is shown as branch gone; a failed remote lookup is shown with its reason. Empty sections are omitted and the summary counts every section. Finalize and sweep still use discover_worktrees and see only canonical worktrees. Ref #3386.

  • feat(worktree-status): count every issue-branch type as development

Per the approved design change, Development now holds any worktree on a feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/ or chore/ branch that carries an issue number, using branch_names.is_valid_issue_branch as the single source of truth. An issue prefix without a number, or an unknown prefix, stays in Other / unknown. Ref #3386.

  • resolve CI versions from the published window with one resolver (#3393) Add lib/versions: window.py loads the schema-1 window.json that vergil-containers publishes at the repo's [dependencies].vergil ref (VRG_VERSION_WINDOW= overrides it; any fetch or parse failure raises WindowError naming the URL and the override, with no cached or built-in fallback), and resolve.py implements the spec 6.3 rules once: library vs app from repository-type, whole window vs newest when unpinned, pins must lie in the window, app multi-pins warn (STRICT_APP_PINS flips them fatal later), family-keyed languages must pin, and [ci].primary-version must name a resolved version. extensions/ holds the empty per-language registry.

    Add vrg-ci-resolve (--format json|github-output) for derive.sh. [ci].versions becomes optional; _DEFAULT_VERSIONS, primary_ci_version, _default_ci_versions and the cpp/node tag parsers are removed. The dev container image, vrg-validate (a new config check), the integration-test gates and repo-init's release container now all resolve through the resolver, and new repos get no [ci].versions. Ref vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3367.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• remove Ruby support from the tooling (#3388) Ruby is dropped from the language lifecycle (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec section 9) and its only consumer is archived, so its support is dead code. Remove it from the primary-language enum, the language registry, version detection and bumping, repo-init scaffolding and cd-release secrets, container image and Gemfile detection, cache and warmup files, semgrep rulesets, the CodeQL and action-pattern sets, vrg-generate-commands, and the gitignore fragment, together with the packaged license_finder config and the tests that covered them.

A vergil.toml that still declares primary-language = "ruby" now fails with a ConfigError naming the retirement, instead of the generic warn-and-treat-as-unset path that would have validated it silently as a language-less repo.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• honour VRG_VERSION_WINDOW inside the dev container (#3402) When VRG_VERSION_WINDOW is set on the host, vrg-container-run resolves it to an absolute path, fails on the host (naming the path) if it is empty, not an existing file, or contains ':', bind-mounts the file read-only at /run/vergil/version-window.json and points VRG_VERSION_WINDOW in the container at that mount. The env-prefixes passthrough never forwards the raw host value. Unset leaves behaviour unchanged.

  • flush stdout and stderr before exec so the banner survives a pipe or file (#3403) When stdout is not a TTY, Python block-buffers it, and os.execvp replaces the process without flushing, so the run banner printed just before the exec was lost in CI logs and tee captures. Every os.execvp caller under src/ now goes through lib/process.exec_replace, which flushes both streams first. Regression tests model a block-buffered stdout for vrg-container-run and vrg-container-docs, and a subprocess test checks a real exec over a pipe. Ref #3396.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: • make vergil-tooling a library repository, keeping its CI version pin (#3404) vergil-tooling is installed into every consumer's image, so it is a library under the repository-type definitions (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec section 3). As a tooling (app) repo, the resolver would narrow its packaged-Python matrix to a single version once derive.sh calls it, leaving its coverage gate on one interpreter. A library with a pin resolves to exactly the pin, so [ci].versions keeps 3.14/3.13/3.12 and the app multi-pin warning goes away. Pin removal stays with #3371.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add the Python resolver extension, toolchain-selection and floor checks (#3401) A packaged Python app resolves to the newest window version with a published vergil-python runtime, and fails loud when none has one; a packaged library keeps its whole matrix and only its deployed runtime needs a published package. [package.python].runtime becomes optional: unset, the builder derives the x.y runtime (vergil-python at /opt/vergil/python/); set, its x.y must be in the window. vrg-validate warns on a requires-python or go.mod floor below the window and an upper bound that excludes its newest version, and fails on .python-version or uv python-preference. vrg-container-run passes UV_PYTHON= into the container. Language rules live only in lib/versions/extensions/{python,go}.py; floors.py dispatches. Ref vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3368

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• resolve --epic adhoc against the task repo and scope adhoc-epic ensure to the target owner (#3412) vrg-epic-move resolved the adhoc sentinel against the cwd repo, so a task in another repo was linked under the wrong ad-hoc epic. It now resolves against the task's own repo. vrg-adhoc-epic ensure minted a cwd-scoped App token, so a private repo in another org could not be resolved; it now runs under github.target_org(owner). vrg-issue-create already resolved adhoc against --repo under the right owner; its test now asserts that. Ref #3409.

  • resolve a bare --epic #N against the task's epic home, not the cwd repo (#3416) A bare epic ref was parsed against the cwd repo, so running from a code repo looked up the wrong issue. resolve_epic_ref now reads a bare #N against the task repo's epic home (new epics.qualify_epic_ref, built on resolve_epic_home): /.github for a public repo, the repo itself for a self-homed private one. A qualified owner/repo#N is unchanged and needs no network call. vrg-epic-move now resolves the epic against the task repo (and its cross-org guard no longer rejects a bare ref for a task in another org); vrg-epic-link resolves its bare epic against the task and runs the home and visibility probes under the task owner's token; vrg-issue-create already passed --repo and gains documented help. Ref #3411.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: • follow the version window: remove the [ci].versions pin (#3408) vergil-tooling is a library repository (#3400), so with no pin vrg-ci-resolve gives it the whole published Python window (3.14, 3.13, 3.12). Also drop the <4.0 upper bound from requires-python, keeping the 3.12 floor (spec section 6.4), and update the CLAUDE.md and ci-architecture text that said the matrix comes from [ci].versions. Task 15a of epic vergil-project/.github#407. Ref #3371

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• allow uv python-preference and pin the interpreter source in containers (#3413) python-preference picks the interpreter's source (managed or system), not its version, so the toolchain check no longer reports it; .python-version stays an error. The Python container env now sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system next to UV_PYTHON, which uv ranks above pyproject.toml and uv.toml settings, so a repo's only-managed can never make a Vergil container download its own interpreter. vrg-container-test now passes the same env as vrg-container-run. Spec 6.5 amendment, epic vergil-project/.github#407.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• run the cache build's warmup with the resolver's UV_PYTHON and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE (#3422) The cached-image build ran its setup step (vergil-tooling install, build-command, warmup) with uv's defaults plus the repo's own settings, so a repo with python-preference = "only-managed" and no .python-version made uv download a managed interpreter instead of using the image's. ensure_cached_image now takes a required build_env, the same container_env(resolution) the run path passes; the setup step exports it before every fragment (in the shell, so it is not baked into the committed image), and it is folded into the cache key so a change of resolved version or source rebuilds. An empty env adds nothing to the key, so languages without a container env keep their existing caches. vrg-container-run, vrg-container-cache (build and status) and provision_dev_image pass it.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• build failed-command messages from CalledProcessError fields (#3438) Python 3.15 changed str(subprocess.CalledProcessError): an argv list is no longer quoted. User-facing messages were built from that stdlib text, so they changed between interpreters and test_vrg_package failed on 3.15.

Add lib/process_errors.py: command_text (moved from update_deps/failure.py), failure_message, failure_detail and error_text, which build the message from cmd, returncode, stderr and stdout. GitHubAPIError.str now uses failure_detail, so every handler that prints a GitHubAPIError is version-independent too. Route every site that interpolated str() or {exc} of a CalledProcessError through the helper, and assert the helper's own format in the tests.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• pin uv to the docs image's Python in vrg-container-docs (#3448) A Python repo's docs build now sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system, matching the CI docs jobs (vergil-actions#1002). A repo with python-preference = "only-managed" can no longer make uv fetch, or fail to find, a managed interpreter. Docs builds resolve no version, so only the source is pinned, through the new source_env() in the Python resolver extension, which container_env() now builds on. There is no fallback: if the image's Python misses requires-python, uv fails loudly. Ref #3414

  • use the repo's ad-hoc epic when the sweep epic is in another org (#3450)

  • surface an unreadable vergil.toml in the managed-file renders (#3453) dependabot.resolve_language and repo_config._gitignore_language no longer turn a ConfigError into None. An absent vergil.toml or undeclared language still resolves to None. vrg-dependabot-sync and vrg-gitignore-sync exit 2 with the config error and write nothing, which the fleet sweep records as a per-repo error row. The local gitignore audit reports an explicit failure instead of judging the fence against a silent base-only language. Ref #3451

  • recognise local reusable-workflow calls in the CI-gates guard (#3457) _CI_USES_RE required a trailing @, so a ci.yml that calls its reusable workflows by local path (uses: ./.github/workflows/.yml, as vergil-actions does) yielded no caller jobs and apply refused every required context. A local call now maps to the same reusable-workflow name as the remote form. Ref #3454.

  • build against the per-series vergil-python package and derive vergil-tooling's runtime (#3458) The python builder used the full [package.python].runtime value as the package name and install root, so a 3.14.8 pin installed the legacy per-patch vergil-python3.14.8 at /opt/vergil/python/3.14.8. It now installs, builds against and depends on the per-series vergil-python at /opt/vergil/python/ for pinned and derived runtimes. An exact-patch pin is checked against the installed CPython patch and the build fails loudly when the series package serves another one. vergil-tooling drops its own 3.14.8 pin so its runtime is derived from the window. Ref #3455

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• bump the runtime pin from the per-series vergil-python package (#3468)
  • fix(update-deps): bump the runtime pin from the per-series vergil-python package

The vergil updater looked up the legacy per-patch vergil-python package names, so it could not keep an exact [package.python] runtime pin current once vergil-python moved to one package per series, and would fail once the legacy packages leave the index. It now reads the newest version of vergil-python on every build and install-test index, takes its CPython patch (the part before +) and bumps the pin to it within its series. A missing series package, indexes that disagree on the patch, a malformed version, a patch on another series or older than the pin all fail loudly. The legacy-name lookup is removed; the missing-package error explains the retirement. A newer series is still only reported as held back. Ref #3456

  • fix(update-deps): hold the runtime bump back while the package indexes disagree

The deb and rpm indexes publish separately, so right after a vergil-python release they briefly serve different patches. That was a hard failure, which made the next vrg-update-deps run file a fix task for a normal, transient state. The updater now leaves the pin unchanged and records a held-back entry naming each served patch and the indexes serving it until they agree. Every other loud failure is unchanged, and a served patch on another series still fails even while the indexes disagree. Ref #3456

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• omit allow_forking for public org repos (#1585) GitHub only accepts the allow_forking field on org-owned private repos; sending it for a public repo returns 422 ("Allow forks setting can only be changed on org-owned private repositories"), failing the GitHub-config step when adopting public repos like an org .github repo.

Gate allow_forking on visibility: set it only for private org repos and leave it unmanaged (None) for public org repos and user-owned repos. compute_desired_state already has visibility in scope and threads it into desired_repo_settings; the existing None handling in _diff_dataclass and _apply_repo_settings then omits the field from the PATCH body. Private org behaviour and the members_can_fork_private_repositories 422 handler are unchanged.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• mechanized dependency-update workflow (Phase 1) (#1586)
  • docs(specs): add vrg-update-deps design and phase 1 plan (#1379)

Mechanized, human-run dependency-update tool: generic driver + updater registry, managed-worktree execution, Python/uv updater, full PR lifecycle. Phase 1 plan covers the Python end-to-end slice; other updaters and the vrg-release worktree retrofit (#1578) follow. Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add pipeline context and error types

UpdateDepsContext carries repo, repo_root, branch, worktree_path, pr_url, any_changes, and per-updater results through the stage pipeline. UpdateDepsError mirrors ReleaseError. Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add updater protocol, result type, registry

Updater is a runtime-checkable Protocol (applies/apply); UpdateResult reports changed/summary/commit_message/warnings; applicable_updaters filters a registry by applies(). Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add Python/uv language updater

PythonUvUpdater applies when pyproject.toml and uv.lock exist; apply() runs 'uv lock --upgrade' in the dev container and reports changed iff uv.lock is dirty. Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add managed-worktree create/remove helper

create_worktree makes a worktree under .worktrees/ on a new branch off a base ref and rejects an existing path; remove_worktree force-removes it. Shared mechanism for automated workflows (vrg-release retrofit tracked in #1578). Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add preflight with synced-develop checks and worktree creation

Preflight asserts on develop, clean tree, and local develop in sync with origin/develop, then creates the managed worktree off develop and chdirs into it. Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add single-shot validation stage

run_validation runs 'vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate' in the cwd (the worktree) and raises UpdateDepsError with captured output on failure. Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add PR create/merge and worktree-cleanup helpers

prepare_pr pushes the worktree branch and opens the PR to develop; merge_pr reuses pr_merge.wait_and_merge; cleanup_worktree chdirs to the root, removes the worktree, and deletes the local branch (used by both no-op and success paths). Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add stage pipeline with no-op/abort and worktree cleanup

build_stages wires preflight -> update -> validate -> prepare-pr -> merge -> finalize. Updaters commit per category; downstream stages no-op when nothing changed; validate is fail_fast (abort leaves the worktree); finalize removes the worktree on both no-op and success. Ref #1379

  • feat(update-deps): add vrg-update-deps CLI entry point and console script

main() refuses agent identities (human-only), captures repo_root before any worktree chdir, and drives the stage pipeline via progress.run_pipeline. Registers the vrg-update-deps console script. Ref #1379

  • test(update-deps): satisfy lint, typecheck, and 100% coverage gates

Mark Protocol stub bodies and the unused ctx arg with pragma/noqa; move annotation-only Path imports under TYPE_CHECKING; narrow optional ctx in orchestrator tests; add branch/error-path tests so the new modules reach 100% branch coverage under vrg-validate. Ref #1379

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• resolve the python runtime once per release, not per build cell (#3496) vrg-package matrix now resolves the vergil-python runtime once (the pin or the derived series) and records it as runtime on every build cell and in packages-manifest.json. vrg-package build --runtime builds against that recorded value instead of re-reading the version window, so parallel cells can no longer pick different runtimes per architecture (vergil-tooling 2.1.258 shipped vergil-python3.15 on amd64 and 3.14 on arm64). Without --runtime, a local build resolves the runtime itself as before; every build prints the runtime it chose. The new vrg-package check-runtime fails a release whose packages do not all depend on exactly the recorded runtime.

  • accept the resolver's container tag for every language in vrg-release-validate-inputs (#3497) cd-release always passes the resolver's primary-container-tag to validate-inputs (vergil-actions#1017). The CLI refused any --container-tag for cpp and typescript because _CONTAINER_LANGUAGES was a frozen copy of the languages supported when the shell check was ported, and it was never extended when C++ and TypeScript were added. Replace it with a shape check that applies to every language: the tag must be a dotted-numeric version (20 for clang-20, 24 for node-24, 3.14 for python). This still rejects 'latest', a family-prefixed version token such as clang-20, and malformed values. Ref #3494

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• give per-kind advice for deferred publishes (#3561) The deferral comment and the close-finalize message treated every deferred publish as a CD job. A deferred package-index now gets advice to re-run (or wait for) the publish-index workflow in the org's packages repo, resolved from [package].vendor, and to confirm the release's packages appear in the index. CD jobs keep their advice, both are given when both kinds are deferred, and the do-not-resume warning stays (#3543).

  • remove the retired triage/idea/research labels and have the sync delete them (#3564) Drop the three retired intake kind labels from data/labels.json, and make vrg-ensure-label --sync delete them (alongside the registry's delete list) from any repo that still has them. The retired names come from intake_route.RETIRED_LABELS, the single source of truth. Deletion lists the repo's labels first and deletes only those present, so it is idempotent and reports each removal, and a real gh error now propagates instead of being swallowed. Ref #3546

  • audit TypeScript devDependencies, not just production (#3567) The TypeScript AUDIT step drops --omit=dev, so npm audit checks every package in package-lock.json, devDependencies included. A vulnerable docs or test tool now fails the gate. The license summary stays production-only. Refs #3552

  • replace and verify the parent after a cross-repo one-off transfer (#3569) A transfer carries the intake parent across, sometimes only after a delay, so the post-transfer link either failed (Sub issue may only have one parent) or was silently overwritten. The transfer path now links with replaceParent, waits, re-reads the native parent and replaces it again if it reverted, failing loudly with a vrg-epic-move fix after bounded rounds. The recreate path links and verifies once. Ref #3556

  • resolve a bare --epic #N against the current repo's epic home (#3572) vrg-epic-audit --epic parsed a bare #N against the cwd repo, so from a public code repo it looked up the wrong issue. Qualify it with epics.qualify_epic_ref against the current repo, giving /.github#N for a public repo and the repo itself for a self-homed private one. The visibility probe runs under the current repo owner's App token. A full owner/repo#N is used as written, with no lookup. Ref #3415

  • re-poll suspected orphaned check-runs for a grace period before failing (#3574) During a GitHub Actions incident, job results are written back late, which looks identical to an orphaned check-run at the moment of checking. The check waiter (vrg-finalize-pr, vrg-release) and vrg-pr-await declared an orphan after one minute or immediately, advising a close/reopen that discarded results already on their way.

    • A check pending over a completed run is now a suspected orphan, re-polled (job re-read every 30s) for VRG_ORPHAN_GRACE seconds (default 300) with a warning naming the suspects. A result arriving in the window finishes the wait normally; only an expired suspect raises OrphanedCheckError, naming how long each check waited.

    • retry an empty head-SHA run lookup before failing the evidence gate (#3575) GitHub's run-by-SHA index can trail a just-completed CI run, which failed the vergil-containers 2.1.30 release gate although the run existed. harvest now re-queries an empty lookup with backoff for a bounded grace period (--run-grace-secs, default 300s, inside the step's 15-min timeout), logging each retry, then fails with a message naming the wait. A visible failed or in-progress run still fails at once. Ref #3434

    • stage docs sources like CI before mkdocs runs (#3576) vrg-container-docs now runs vrg-docs-stage and vrg-docs-patch-nav on the host before mkdocs, matching CI's docs staging, so local strict builds pass or fail where CI does. The nav patch goes to a gitignored sibling copy (mkdocs.staged.yml); the tracked mkdocs.yml is never rewritten. The generated paths are added to the managed base gitignore, and the command refuses before writing when any generated path is not ignored (e.g. a committed staged copy). Missing gh auth fails the command; staging is never skipped. Adds git.is_ignored (check-ignore). Ref #3439

    • add vrg-container-cache prune for finished-branch cache images (#3577)

    • fix(container-cache): add vrg-container-cache prune for finished-branch cache images

    Cached per-branch images piled up on agent VMs because vrg-finalize-pr only cleans the machine it runs on (#3481). The new prune subcommand keeps an image whose sanitized branch matches a live branch (local, worktree or origin) in any repo of the repo set, removes the rest, and never touches protected branches or images a container uses. Dry run by default; --apply removes and fails loudly on rmi errors. The multi-repo live-branch lookup lives in lib/live_branches.py for reuse by #3566.

    • fix(container-cache): fall back to tracking refs when a repo's origin is unreadable

    On a Lima VM the default repo set is the whole mounted projects tree, which includes private repos the agent's App cannot ls-remote, so one unreadable origin aborted every prune. Such a repo now contributes its local refs/remotes/origin/* instead, with a warning naming the repo and the error. Tracking refs are stale only toward listing deleted branches, so the fallback keeps more, never less. Any other git failure still stops the run.

    • test(container-cache): wrap long prune test signatures for lint and ty

    • ensure the in-progress label in a planning item's own repo (#3578) ensure_planning_epic ensured 'in-progress' only in the planning queue home, so a member-repo item moved into planning could not be labelled by epic-create ('in-progress' not found). It now also ensures the label in the target (item) repo, deduplicated when the two coincide. Every entry into planning (the planning sentinel in vrg-epic-move and vrg-issue-create, and vrg-intake-route planning) already passes the item's repo here, so this one change covers all three. Ref #3520

    • record relay submissions on the local worktree (#3579) A branch submitted by name that is already on origin went down the relay path, which opened the PR but never recorded it. When that branch also had a local ready worktree, its state stayed ready with no submission, so the freeze refused pr-watch fix commits and pushes. Record the submission on the local worktree after any successful live open; branches without a local worktree are unchanged. Ref #3525

    • preflight refuses on main/develop divergence with a recovery path (#3580) A fresh vrg-release now fetches main and refuses before anything is cut when origin/main has commits not on origin/develop, naming the commits and the recovery: vrg-release --resume for a release stopped before its back-merge, else a manual back-merge PR merged with a merge commit. Develop ahead of main stays normal; a resume skips the check; a failed fetch or compare refuses. Ref #3527

    • preview the real per-repo verdict in a sweep dry run (#3585) In dry-run mode run_sweep now runs each applicator check-only in a disposable detached probe worktree and reports the verdict a live run would reach (ready, skipped, or a follow-up) instead of reporting every repo ready. The Applicator seam gains a check keyword: the xdist and ci.yml applicators compute the verdict without writing (xdist runs no uv lock), the dependabot target previews with vrg-dependabot-sync --check, and the gitignore target runs --write inside the discarded probe because vrg-gitignore-sync --check is stricter than --write. The xdist sweep also treats a repo that is not a Python repo as out of scope, so it no longer files follow-up issues against docs or container repos. Ref #3549

    • file a fix task when an updater or hook fails (#3586) An update-kind failure (an updater or the repo hook failing before validation) opened no PR and filed no fix task, so it was recorded only in run output and the release tracking comment. fix_task_stage now files a fix task for every failure. For an update failure the task stands on its own: it names the failing updater (recorded on DepsFailure.updater), carries the error and output, and says how to reproduce it on develop and where to cut the fix branch. failure_summary names the fix task for update failures too, and failure_markdown no longer tells the reader to reproduce on a branch that was never pushed. Docs updated to match. Ref #3550

    • scan the C++ conan audit in the lock's Debug configuration (#3587) conan audit scan already covers test_requires and tool_requires (every non-root graph node, both contexts) and implicitly loads conan.lock, but it resolved the default Release profile, so locked packages a recipe requires only in Debug (the build_type conan lock create and INSTALL use) were never scanned. Pin -s build_type=Debug and pass --lockfile=conan.lock explicitly on both AUDIT conan steps so the scan matches the lock and a missing lock fails instead of re-resolving. Verified against Conan 2.33 with a test recipe.

    • give the human exact commands to resolve a submitted PR's merge conflict (#3589) A conflict on an already-submitted PR can only be resolved by the human: the branch is frozen to agents. vrg-finalize-pr now replaces the generic advice with the worktree path (or how to create one), fetch, merge of the base branch (not a rebase, since the PR is public), validation, raw-git commit and push, and the re-run. pr_merge raises a MergeConflictError subclass so other callers are unaffected. Ref #3555.

    • defer a package-index miss before close-finalize so the tracking issue stays open (#3596) Move the package-index stage ahead of close-finalize so an index-only timeout reaches the deferral comment and leaves the tracking issue open, as a CD publish deferral does. A stage that records its own failure as a publish deferral is no longer added to the halted-stage list, so close-finalize does not mistake it for a resumable failure. The publish-status and consumer-refresh hold messages now use publish_deferred_remedy for per-kind advice. Ref #3557.

    • comment on the open fix task instead of filing a duplicate on a re-run (#3597) Before filing a fix task, look for an open one with the same version-keyed title and the same failure kind (its '## Failure: ' heading). If one exists, add the new failure to it as a comment and link that task from the PR body and run summary. A failed or malformed lookup fails loud rather than risk a duplicate. Ref #3560.

    • run the image's mkdocs when a Python repo has no docs dependency group (#3598) vrg-container-docs ran 'uv sync --group docs' for every repo with a pyproject.toml, so a repo with no docs group (vergil-tooling itself) failed with uv's 'Group docs is not defined'. CI's docs jobs sync no group: they run 'uv run mkdocs', which falls through to the docs image's mkdocs-material. Match that: sync the docs group only when pyproject.toml declares one, otherwise run plain 'uv run mkdocs' and print a note saying the image's mkdocs is used. An unparseable pyproject.toml now fails with a clear error before the container starts.

    • keep other repos' branch images in finalize's prune; report rmi failures (#3599) vrg-finalize-pr's orphan-image sweep now asks the platform repo set (the same live-branch lookup and plan_prune verdicts as vrg-container-cache prune) instead of the finalized repo's local branches, so it no longer deletes other repos' in-progress images. It is skipped, with a message, where no repo set can be confirmed (the physical host), and a failed lookup or rmi is a warning, never a failed finalize. clean_branch_images and the sweep move to lib/cache_prune.py and return their rmi failures; vrg-container-cache clean and clean-all name each failed image with the runtime's error and exit 1. Ref #3566

    • make vrg-gitignore-sync --check and --write agree (#3600)

    • fix(gitignore): make vrg-gitignore-sync --check drift exactly when --write would change the file

      • --write now removes exact repeats of the fence's own patterns outside the fence (the fence is the single source of truth), and --check now flags a fence that is not first, a missing trailing newline, and any other layout --write would rewrite. --write then --check always passes. Ref #3568.

      • fix(fleet-sync): preview the gitignore target with vrg-gitignore-sync --check

      With --check and --write consistent, the gitignore dry run no longer needs to write inside the probe worktree; drop check_predicts_write. Ref #3568.

      • self-heal a conflicting release PR by merging main into it (#3601) When the release PR is CONFLICTING, merge-release now merges origin/main into the release branch in its worktree and pushes it, then waits again (bounded to 3 attempts). A conflict in CHANGELOG.md alone is resolved by keeping the release branch's generated changelog; any other conflicted path aborts the merge and stops with the exact commands to resolve it by hand. Re-runs are idempotent: an already-merged main is not merged again, and a local merge a prior run did not push is pushed. Refs #3526.

      • say whether close-finalize closed the tracking issue or left it open (#3609) The close-finalize completion comment always read 'Tracking issue closed. Repository finalized.', even when a deferred publish (CD jobs or package-index) or a halted earlier stage left the issue open. It now mirrors close_and_finalize's branches and names each deferred kind. Ref #3593

      • skip gitignored files in the common lint checks (#3610) vrg-container-docs build copies the gitignored release notes and changelog into docs/site/docs/, and the common markdownlint check then linted them, failing the next vrg-validate until they were deleted by hand. Every file list the common checks discover (markdownlint, shellcheck, yamllint, hadolint) now drops the paths the repo's .gitignore excludes, via a new batched git.ignored_paths (one git check-ignore --stdin call). Tracked files are always kept, and a check-ignore failure raises rather than linting less. Ref #3594

      • self-home a private repo whose owner has no .github (#3614) resolve_epic_home crashed with a traceback for a personal-account repo with no /.github: the .github visibility probe failed with 'Could not resolve to a Repository'. A private repo whose owner has no .github now homes its epics in itself (there is no central home). Only GitHub's not-found answer counts as absent; every other probe failure raises EpicHomeError, which cli_main prints as a one-line ': ' instead of a traceback. A missing token keeps its own error. The not-found classification is factored out of repo_exists as github.is_repo_not_found. Docs record the new row of the epic-home rule.

      • fail validation cleanly when the image rebuild fails (#3616)

      • fix(finalize-pr): report a failed cache re-provision as a warning instead of a stage failure

        • When validation's container fails to launch, finalize rebuilds the dev image and retries. A failed rebuild (the low-disk guard refusing it, a failed cache build or commit, or an unresolvable version window) now prints a warning naming the image, the full error text and the retry command, marks the validation stage warn, and skips the retry, instead of failing the stage with a raw exception after the merge has landed. Ref #3605

        • fix(finalize-pr): fail validation when the dev-image rebuild fails

        An unrun validation is an unknown result, not a pass (#3316). A failed rebuild now raises FinalizeError naming the image, the full original error text and the retry command, so the validation stage is recorded failed and vrg-finalize-pr exits non-zero, while the CD check and final summary still run. The pointless second validation attempt is still skipped. Ref #3605

        • guard branch creation through vrg-git branch (#3617) vrg-git branch , and its -c/-C copy and -m/-M rename forms, now apply the same issue-branch name-format check and open-task guard as worktree add -b, checkout -b and switch -c. Listing, deleting, upstream and description forms pass through unchanged. Renames are covered because renaming to an issue-branch name creates that branch as surely as creating it; renames to non-issue names are unaffected. Ref #3606

        • fail org-wide vrg-queue and vrg-epic-audit clearly when /.github is missing (#3618) Add epics.require_org_home, which probes /.github with github.repo_exists before the org-wide paths of vrg-queue and vrg-epic-audit use it. A missing .github raises a one-line EpicHomeError saying there is no org-wide queue or epic home and pointing at --repo; any other probe failure is an EpicHomeError carrying the API error, and a missing token keeps its own message. Ref #3613.

Document the security-settings half of the config audit, where vrg-dependabot-audit runs, and the dependabot.yml scaffolding. Ref #3423.

Add it to the nav and link it from the permission-model and identity-architecture guides.

Refresh the attribute table to match the CLI. Ref #3595

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• allow pr update-branch for the USER identity (#3559) gh pr update-branch [--rebase] updates a PR branch onto its base server-side, with no checkout or force-push. Add it to the user/human pr allowlist; it stays off the audit allowlist because it writes. Tests cover both identities, and the permission-model guide lists it. Ref #3542

  • redirect agents to vrg-pr-workflow report-ready from --help (#3562) Run the agent identity gate before argument parsing so an agent's --help reaches it and prints a human-only redirect to vrg-pr-workflow report-ready instead of the usage. The refusal message for other agent invocations now names the same handoff. Human --help is unchanged. Ref #3545

  • add index --check-config to validate packages.toml without building (#3565) Loads packages.toml through the index config parser and exits non-zero with the PackageError message on any invalid value, using no network, keys or output directory. --keys and --out stay required for a real build, enforced with an argparse error. Ref #3551.

  • allow run rerun and read-only workflow/cache commands (#3573) Allow run rerun for the user agent so it can retry a failed CI job. Allow workflow list/view and cache list for every identity, audit included, since they only read CI configuration and state. Deny workflow run for every identity with an explanatory refusal: dispatching a workflow can start CD or a release, which is a human action. Bring the vrg-gh allowlist and deny tables in the permission-model guide into line with the code. Ref #3420

  • stream the publish-index run in the package-index stage (#3581) The package-index stage now finds the earliest non-cancelled Publish package index run in /packages created since the CD release job started, streams it with watch_workflow, and follows the next run when one is cancelled. Whenever no run is streamed it prints a heartbeat per poll. Run-following is progress output only: a gh failure there falls back to polling, and the index poll remains the sole pass/fail check under the single deadline. Ref #3528

  • add day x repo summary, per-day pages and --repo filter (#3582) vrg-activity-log gains --out-dir, which writes index.md (a day x repo table of closed-issue counts), days/.md (that day's issues grouped by repo) and repos/.md (each repo's flat ledger), and --repo, which prints one repo's flat ledger. The default stdout output is unchanged so the nightly docs refresh keeps working. The search limit rises from 100 to gh's 1000 cap, with a stderr warning when it is hit, since a truncated window would leave the summary's older rows silently empty. Ref #3544.

  • add --all-versions to run the coverage gate on every CI version (#3583) vrg-validate --all-versions (Python only) adds one test stage per version vrg-ci-resolve resolves, after the test stage. Each stage has uv install the version as a managed interpreter, syncs the dev group into its own environment under the temp dir, and runs the unchanged pytest --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 gate with its reports redirected beside that environment. The container interpreter's own version is skipped, as the plain test stage covers it. Non-Python languages and --check values other than test are refused. The default vrg-validate is unchanged. Ref #3547

  • report undeclared ruleset parameters as a distinct audit category (#3584) A live ruleset rule parameter that the desired rule of the same type does not declare, and that is not strip-listed, is now reported as an UndeclaredParam naming the ruleset, rule type, key and live value, with guidance to declare it on/off in the spec or add it to _STRIP_RULE_PARAMS. Undeclared keys are removed from the value comparison so they no longer surface as opaque .rules drift. They keep the audit NON-COMPLIANT; apply still converges value drift but cannot resolve them (GitHub re-applies its default) and exits 1.

  • add an OSV-Scanner vulnerability audit to the Java profile (#3588) The Java AUDIT stage only resolved the dependency tree and checked licenses; nothing compared dependencies against an advisory database. It now writes a CycloneDX SBOM of the whole reactor (every module and scope, test included) with the cyclonedx-maven-plugin, then scans it with osv-scanner, failing on any known vulnerability. A repo-root osv-scanner.toml holds reviewed suppressions, and a dev image without osv-scanner fails with a message naming the fix instead of skipping. Ref #3554

  • refuse epic/archive-labelled issues where a task is expected (#3591) Add epics.non_task_kind / non_task_ref_kind / non_task_refusal_message, a shared label-based test and refusal text for an epic or archive given where a task is expected. report-ready and vrg-submit-pr now refuse archives as well as epics through it, and vrg-epic-link --task and vrg-issue-create --blocked-by gain the same guard (fail closed on a failed label read). Ref #2842

  • auto-prune per-branch cache images when the image store runs low (#3607) Before a cached dev image is built, read the free space of the image store's filesystem. Below VRG_CACHE_PRUNE_FREE_GB (default 10 GB, 0 disables) run the same prune as vrg-container-cache prune --apply against the same repo set, printing each removed image. A host with no repo set is not guessed; prune failures and refused rmi are warnings. The build then continues only with at least 3 GB (or the threshold, if lower) free, otherwise it stops with the numbers and the manual command. Ref #3571

  • refuse epic, archive and closed issues when creating an issue branch (#3608) vrg-git worktree add -b, checkout -b and switch -c now read issue (state and labels in one gh call) for a /- branch and refuse it when the issue is closed or labelled epic/archive, using the shared epics.non_task_refusal_message. A failed or malformed read refuses with an actionable message. Adds epics.non_task_kind_of_labels so the label check is reused without a second lookup. Ref #3592

  • report-ready pushes the branch itself, not just the relay ref (#3612) report-ready now pushes the reported commit to origin/ (setting upstream) before recording anything, so callers no longer need a separate push. A GitHub workflow-permission refusal is reported as expected and the state is still recorded; any other push failure fails with no local state and no relay ref. A re-run on a frozen branch whose HEAD drifted is refused before pushing. The workflow-refusal matcher moves to lib.git so vrg-git and report-ready share it. Ref #3602

  • prune finished cache images inside the VM on vrg-vm update (#3615) After the reinstall, vrg-vm update (and each box of --all) runs the box's own vrg-container-cache prune --apply over the existing transport. Lima boxes get their identity's projects_dir as --root because the in-guest default needs a checkout cwd; off-platform boxes use their default /vergil/projects. A probe tells a missing or pre-prune vrg-container-cache apart from a real failure and skips with a warning. A failed prune prints its output and exit loudly but never fails the update. --no-prune opts out. Ref #3604
